docs.title: fdia-graph
docs.text:
Stealthy FDIA localization datasets for power grids, PyTorch-ready in one line. Eight IEEE systems (14 / 30 / 57 / 89 / 118 / 145 / 200 / 300 buses), one continuous timeline of 72,000 frames each: a record table when shuffled, a time series when not.

import fdia_graph as fg

ds = fg.load("ieee118", split="train")     # auto-downloads + caches
for batch in ds.loader(batch_size=64):
    batch["node_x"], batch["edge_x"], batch["edge_index"], batch["y"], batch["family"]

ts = fg.load("ieee118", split="test", order="time")   # the same frames in time order
Xw, yw = ts.windows(W=24, stride=12)                  # [n, 24, N, 4] windows for an LSTM / TGN

Read To learn docs/ROADMAP.md which file does what, and how the paths connect docs/guides/generation.md how a timeline is generated, and which layers a feature may read docs/reference/DATA_DICTIONARY.md what every array means docs/reference/GLOSSARY.md every term, with where it lives in the code docs/reference/MODULES.md what every file does, in one line docs/reference/CONCEPTS_TO_CODE.md paper equations to functions docs/reference/CLASS_MAP.md architecture: the UML class and module diagrams, drawn from the code docs/reference/EXAMPLES.md runnable baselines, the timeline as sequences, dataset stats docs/analysis/estimation/ · docs/analysis/localization/ · docs/analysis/trust/ · docs/analysis/federated/ the analysis modules, with results CONTRIBUTING.md rules, pull-request flow, releases

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
command gives pip install fdia-graph the loader (numpy, h5py) pip install "fdia-graph[torch]" + PyTorch DataLoader pip install "fdia-graph[pyg]" + torch_geometric records and timelines pip install "fdia-graph[generate]" + pandapower, to generate custom data pip install "fdia-graph[iso]" + gridstatus, to download CAISO and ERCOT load profiles (NYISO needs no extra) pip install "fdia-graph[all]" every extra above pip install fdia-analysis the analysis toolkit, a second package on top of this one: state estimation, localization, federated training, trusted-meter selection (its extras: [se], [torch], [federated], [all])

The repository holds two toolkits. fdia-graph (the package fdia_graph, under src/) generates a timeline and loads it, and is everything above. fdia-analysis (the package fdia_analysis, under analysis/) is what is measured on a timeline; it depends on fdia-graph, and fdia-graph never imports it.

Data is pinned per SDK version and cached in ~/.cache/fdia_graph. fg.load(..., release="v0.8.1") pins a data version, any timeline release from v0.8.0; pip install --upgrade fdia-graph moves it forward. The record shards of the data releases before v0.8.0 are read by fdia-graph==0.21.0.

docs.title: Load
docs.text:
One file per system, one loader. order decides what the file is to you:

fg.load("ieee300", split="train")                              # 60/20/20 chronological split, episodes never cut
fg.load("ieee118", split="test", families=["At"])             # family subset
fg.load("ieee118", units="pu")                                 # per-unit + radians (default: physical)
fg.load("ieee118", order="random", seed=0)                     # the record table: a fixed permutation
fg.load("ieee118", split="test", order="time")                 # the time series: windows, episodes
you want call a whole split at once ds.export() (arrays), ds.export(format="torch"), ds.export(format="pandas") windows for an LSTM / TGN ds.windows(W, stride, label, layer, per_bus=True) on a time-ordered view (one sequence per bus) the attack episodes ds.episodes (onset, length, family, buses) the attack removed every record carries benign and edge_benign next to node_x and clean custom data fg.generate(system, name, attacked_frac=..., families=..., frames=...), then fg.load(name)

docs.title: State estimation
docs.text:
The analysis toolkit, pip install "fdia-analysis[se]":

from fdia_analysis.models.config import PriorConfig
from fdia_analysis.se.methods import SubspacePrior

train, test = fg.load("ieee118", split="train"), fg.load("ieee118", split="test")
est = SubspacePrior(prior=PriorConfig(rank_frac=0.5, reweight="huber", c=2.5)).fit(train)
xhat = est.estimate(test)          # [n, 2N-1] = [theta rad (non-slack) | V pu (all buses)]
print(est.score(test))             # per-family angle / voltage MAE vs the clean truth

One solver, six estimators that each change one thing: WLS, AdaptiveWeighting, ResidualRemoval, SubspacePrior, JacobianWeighting, GatedPrior. Results: docs/analysis/estimation/.

docs.title: Localization
docs.text:
from fdia_analysis.localization.learned import BusCNN             # needs fdia-analysis[torch]
from fdia_analysis.localization.methods import SwingThreshold     # numpy only
from fdia_analysis.models.config import LocalizerConfig

loc = SwingThreshold(localizer=LocalizerConfig(fa_target=0.01)).fit(train)     # per-bus thresholds from benign records only
flag = loc.localize(test)                           # [n, N] bool: which buses are called attacked
print(loc.score(test))                              # per-family node-F1, strict accuracy, DR next to FA

zs = dict(families=[0, 1, 2])                       # the papers' zero-shot protocol
cnn = BusCNN().fit(fg.load("ieee118", split="train", **zs), val=fg.load("ieee118", split="val", **zs))

One calibration, five localizers: SwingThreshold, DeltaThreshold, ResidualLocalizer, BusMLP, BusCNN. Results: docs/analysis/localization/.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
Each record is a sparse measurement graph with N buses (nodes) and E branches (edges). A shape reads "values per item": [N,4] is 4 numbers per bus.

field shape columns meaning node_x [N,4] |V|, P_inj, Q_inj, theta bus meters (node_m is the mask) edge_x [E,2] P_from, Q_from branch flows (edge_m is the mask) edge_index [2,E] from_bus; to_bus connectivity edge_attr [E,8] r, x, b, g, gs, bs, tap, shift static line physics (Data.edge_phys in PyG) y [N] 1 attacked, 0 clean family scalar 0 benign, 1 Aq, 2 Ad, 3 As, 4 Ar, 5 At, 6 Al, 7 Am (fg.FAMILIES) temporal_delta, swing [N,2] ΔP, ΔQ change against the previous frame, and as a z-score of recent change benign, edge_benign [N,4], [E,2] as above the same scan with the attack removed, noise kept clean, edge_clean, edge_clean_full [N,4], [E,2], [E,2] as above noiseless truth: buses, metered branches, every branch seq_id, timestep, split scalars episode index (-1 benign), frame index, partition slack, ybus, yf, yt dataset attributes reference bus, admittance matrices

Full reference: docs/reference/DATA_DICTIONARY.md.

docs.title: Attacks
docs.text:
family attack classical BDD plausibility At slow load ramp, re-solved locally every frame; by default (min_tamper=True) on the support that tampers the fewest devices, else on the region within hops evades peak 2.4% to 5.2% of the load (0.2% per frame over a 12 to 26 frame rise), 60 frames Am the overload attack of [WU26]: a line's reported flow driven to its rating (1.25 times its peak pool flow, or PGLib-OPF's) over the episode on the fewest-tamper support evades the rating reached at the last scan; every scan one AC state, the fewest devices beyond [WU26]'s noise

The generator makes these two multi-snapshot families. The single-snapshot families of data releases v0.8.3 and earlier (Aq load rescale, Al load redistribution, and the in-place Ad bias, As scaling and Ar replay) stay in those files and load, filter and score by name as before (fg.load(..., release="v0.8.3", families=["Aq"])); fdia-graph 0.20 is the last version that generates them.

Every stealthy family is a local false state: the attacker solves the power flow of a subnetwork around the attack with the boundary voltages held true, writes only that subnetwork's meters, and the measurement vector stays consistent with an AC state, so the residual test sees noise. The meters written are the tamper masks in the file's attack/ group. The generated At and Am satisfy equations (13)-(23) of [WU26] (the SCADA measurements, the PMU voltage magnitudes, angles and branch currents, and the operating limits); Am also meets the line-overload goal, eqs. (24)-(25), and both are held on the support that tampers the fewest devices, eq. (12), when min_tamper=True (the default for At; Am always picks its support that way, by the search or by [WU26]'s row reduction, am_attack=OverloadSettings(support_method="rref")). The single-snapshot families and the redistribution Am of the older releases were drawn at random targets, on meters without branch currents, and drove no line to its limit.

Bad-data statistic relative to the alarm threshold, per family, on data release v0.8.3. Green families are indistinguishable from benign; red ones trip the alarm. Meter error follows an accuracy-class model (per-meter bias plus per-scan jitter). Report per-family node-F1 next to the false-alarm rate, never accuracy.

docs.title: Repo roadmap
docs.text: Two toolkits in one repository. The generation toolkit, the distribution fdia-graph and the package fdia_graph (under src/), generates a timeline and loads it: its loader runs on the base install, and its engine (power flow, meters, attacks) needs [generate]. The analysis toolkit, the distribution fdia-analysis and the package fdia_analysis (under analysis/), is what is measured on a timeline: state estimation, localization, federated training, trusted-meter selection and the results store's code. It depends on fdia-graph; nothing in fdia_graph imports it (tests/test_toolkit_boundary.py). The public surface is fg.* and the New York grid (fdia_graph.generation.nygrid, behind [ny]) in the first, and fdia_analysis.se, fdia_analysis.localization, fdia_analysis.trust and fdia_analysis.federated in the second; everything else serves them.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
Every package has one page that says what each of its files does, and tools/layout.py checks that the page names them all. The one-line summary of every file of the repository is reference/MODULES.md, generated from the docstrings.

The generation toolkit, src/fdia_graph/:

file or folder what it is __init__.py the public API; the heavy helpers resolve lazily so load() never imports torch or pandapower errors.py every error the package raises on purpose, defined there registry.py, download.py (name, release) to a download spec with that release's file layout; fetch to ~/.cache/fdia_graph, sha256-verified schema.py the file protocol: every HDF5 group, dataset and attribute name, defined once timeline.py one continuous attacked timeline per system, written as one HDF5 file through the stages of generation/ profiles.py ISO load profiles to AC operating-state pools dataset/ FdiaGraph, composed of graph.py (the static graph), physics.py (admittances, clean flows), records.py (items, collate, DataLoader), export.py (whole-split arrays) and sequence.py (windows, episodes) over dataset/base.py (shared state); clients.py reads a New York timeline as federated clients models/ every value bundle the toolkit passes or returns, one module per subject: fdia_graph/models/base.py (Bundle), fields.py (the field groups bundles share), fdia_graph/models/grid.py, frames.py, plan.py (a timeline's plan and design records), fdia_graph/models/data.py, assets.py; the settings in fdia_graph/models/config.py and the parser inputs in fdia_graph/models/inputs.py, checked by the one engine in fdia_graph/models/validation.py; and the fixed-set arguments in fdia_graph/models/choices.py. A model is imported from its module; the package's __init__.py exports no name. reference/DATA_DICTIONARY.md lists every field ratings/ PGLib-OPF branch ratings of IEEE-14, 118 and 300 formulas/ the mathematics of generation as pure functions with source keys: reference/FORMULAS.md engine/, generation/ the generator: the AC physics, the meters and the attacks, and the stages that walk a timeline: guides/generation.md generation/nygrid/, engine/sensing/ the New York grid and its meters: concepts/new_york_grid.md

The analysis toolkit, analysis/src/fdia_analysis/ (../analysis/README.md):

file or folder what it is se/, localization/, trust/, federated/ the analysis packages, each with its page: analysis/estimation/README.md, analysis/localization/README.md, analysis/trust/README.md, analysis/federated/README.md se/detect/ the alarm rules of the New York grid: concepts/new_york_grid.md results/ the results store's code: ../results/README.md models/ the value bundles only the analysis packages use, on the generation toolkit's Bundle and validation engine: the settings in fdia_analysis/models/config.py, what the analysis formulas accept in fdia_analysis/models/inputs.py, the one rule only they declare in fdia_analysis/models/validation.py, the fixed-set arguments in fdia_analysis/models/choices.py; the score tables in scores.py, the truth an estimator is scored against in fdia_analysis/models/data.py, the estimator's pseudo-measurement records in fdia_analysis/models/grid.py, federated.py (a partition, a round's log), training.py and the results store's records in fdia_analysis.models.results formulas/ the mathematics of analysis as pure functions with source keys: reference/FORMULAS.md

docs.title: The repository
docs.text:
Every folder at the root has one role, and tools/layout.py fails a folder that has none (REPO and DOCS in the tool; the generated table opens reference/MODULES.md).

folder holds src/fdia_graph/ the generation toolkit's package analysis/ the analysis toolkit: its package under analysis/src/fdia_analysis/, its tests under analysis/tests/, its own pyproject.toml tests/ the generation toolkit's test suite, and the helpers both suites share (tests/helpers.py; the fixtures both share are in the root conftest.py) examples/ scripts a user copies results/ the results store: data only, one CSV per experiment and runs.csv, with queries.py pipelines/ the builds of released data: pipelines/newyork/ builds the New York pool and timeline, and holds the MATLAB reference they are checked against tools/ repository tooling only: the gates, the generated docs, pull requests, releases docs/ the documentation, one folder per kind of page (below)

docs.text: folder holds getting-started/ tutorials: new_york_walkthrough.md, one attack day on the New York grid from start to finish guides/ one task each: generation.md (how a timeline is built), state_estimation.md, new_york.md (building the New York data), extending_new_york.md, troubleshooting_new_york.md concepts/ explanations: new_york_grid.md, how the New York grid and its meters are built analysis/ one page per study with its figures and their CSV sidecars: estimation/, localization/, trust/ and federated/ reference/ the file map (MODULES.md), data dictionary, glossary, concepts to code, formulas, examples, benchmarks figures/ shared images with their data sidecars

docs.title: Tests and releases
docs.text: python tools/prereview.py every CI gate, the test suite and the checks CI does not run, on this checkout's source; run before a review is requested (docs/reference/REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md) pytest both suites from the repository root, on this checkout's source (the root pyproject.toml puts src and analysis/src on the path): builds a tiny IEEE-14 timeline in a throwaway cache (about a minute) and checks the documented contracts pytest tests, pytest analysis/tests one toolkit's suite: the generation toolkit's, which runs with fdia_analysis blocked (tests/test_toolkit_boundary.py), or the analysis toolkit's, on the same tiny timeline (the root conftest.py) FDIA_SLOW=1 pytest adds the slow checks: the estimator sanity test on the published IEEE-118 file (the analysis suite) and the longer attack searches (the generation suite) CI tests on Linux (3.12 and 3.9) and Windows, pyright, ruff format and check, the readability gate, the layout gate (tools/layout.py: names, docstrings, package pages, cited names, the repository map, the file map), the generated-docs checks, install on 3.9 and 3.12 release bump PR, then python tools/release.py vX.Y.Z notes.md (tag, GitHub release, PyPI); see CONTRIBUTING.md

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Every release lists what a user of the package can see change. "No user-visible change" means the public API, the generated files and the numbers are the same as the previous release.

docs.title: Unreleased
docs.text:
• One writer owns a timeline file, one record is an episode, and the layers of indirection around them are removed (breaking for the internal names below; no behaviour and no stored byte changed: the five whole-file digests are unchanged, and an IEEE timeline is byte for byte the file the previous code writes). fg.generate, fg.load, generate_timeline, TimelineSource.generate, IeeeSource, NewYorkSource and SingleEpisodeSource are called as before.
  • generation.write.TimelineWriter is the open file of a timeline for both grids and the only place a timeline file is written: TimelineWriter(path, dims, clean, spec), write_graph, header, store, flush, add_episode, finish (the masks, the columns, the episodes, the attributes and, on a file that carries them, the temporal features) and close. A source holds it as source.writer. It replaces start_timeline, create_layers, finish_timeline, timeline_attrs, placement_attrs, _write_masks, _write_episodes, _write_min_rows and _write_am_rows of generation.write; TimelineBuffers, layers and CleanSlice of generation.emit (CleanSlice is now in generation.write); header_attrs, _write_graph, _base_attrs, _static_physics, GRAPH_LEGEND (now in generation.write) and _CHUNK_ROWS of generation; and TimelineSource._finish_file. generation.write.search_attrs is part of IeeeSource._recorded. write_temporal_layers is TimelineWriter.write_temporal_layers (a static method, which trust.secured_copy calls on its own file) and ragged is private to the writer.
  • The steps of the walk are methods of generation.emit.Walk: walk_split, benign_run, ramp_episode, overload_episode, emit_benign and relocate_later (static) were functions of generation.emit. emit.clean_slice is IeeeSource._clean. generation.design.build_generator is FdiaGenerator.from_spec; the worker functions of generation.design are static methods of DesignPool and AmDesigner. engine.attacks.episodes.ramp_step is the method EpisodeDesignMixin.ramp_step only.
  • A New York survey cache (survey_cache) written before this change is not read: its chunks pickled engine.attacks.family.Episode, and the chunks are now named _v2. The survey runs again and saves new chunks beside the old ones.
  • models.plan.Episode is the one record of an attack episode: what a New York family designs (it moved from engine.attacks.family) and a row of every file's episode table. models.data.EpisodeRow and the walk's generation.emit._Episode are gone; Walk.buf is Walk.writer, and Walk.T is gone.
  • models.plan.Planned (a placed episode with its design, its index and its moves) replaces Pending and Designed. Schedule.build is gone: Schedule(...) takes the same arguments. generation.ieee._Planned and IeeeSource._generator are gone (the generator comes from FdiaGenerator.from_spec); AmDesigner is a DesignPool.
  • The designs of an episode are methods of the generator: EpisodeDesignMixin.ramp_design and am_overload_design hold the code of RampDesigner and OverloadDesigner, which are gone with DESIGNERS, Designer and EpisodeDesignMixin.designer. MinimizeMixin.min_tamper chooses between the candidate search and the row reduction itself: SupportStrategy, SearchSupport, MinimizeMixin.support_strategy and RrefSupport.find are gone (RrefSupport.rref_support stays).
  • The loader: the capability tests are written in the dataset.base.CAPABILITIES table (the ten one-line functions are gone); RecordsMixin._add_benign and _add_currents are one method, _add_frame_layers.
  • models.inputs.GeneratedFamilies is a FamilySelection and SupportedSystem a SystemRef.

  • formulas.network: the two Newton solves share the halving of a step (_halved_steps).

  • The analysis toolkit's names are imported from the module that defines them: the eight tables of re-exported names in fdia_analysis are removed (breaking for these import paths; no behaviour, no stored byte and no result number changed). The same change as the generation toolkit's, below. Each package's __init__.py is now its docstring; import fdia_analysis and fdia_analysis.__version__ are unchanged.

  • fdia_analysis.se exports no name: WLS, AdaptiveWeighting, ResidualRemoval, SubspacePrior, JacobianWeighting and GatedPrior come from fdia_analysis.se.methods, SEBase from se.base, JacobianFeatures from se.jacobian. fdia_analysis.se.detect exports none either: AlarmRule and PersistenceRule come from se.detect.rules.
  • fdia_analysis.localization: SwingThreshold, DeltaThreshold and ResidualLocalizer come from localization.methods, BusCNN, BusMLP, LearnedLocalizer, full14 and kcl_residual from localization.learned, LocalizerBase from localization.base.
  • fdia_analysis.federated: FedBusCNN, FedBusMLP and FederatedLocalizer come from federated.localizer, spectral_partition, partition_from_assignment, bus_adjacency and compute_nodes from federated.partition, RegionalPrior from federated.se; Partition and RoundLog from fdia_analysis.models.federated, which defines them.
  • fdia_analysis.trust: TrustedMeters and TrustSelector come from trust.base, TrustedMetersDQN from trust.meter_dqn, secured_copy from trust.secured.
  • fdia_analysis.results: Run comes from results.run, Store from results.store, QUERIES, fill, query and stale from results.docs, cell, figure_data, pivot and table from results.render; METRICS, Better, Metric, Provenance and Record from fdia_analysis.models.results, which defines them.
  • fdia_analysis.models exports no name (__all__ and PUBLIC are gone): from fdia_analysis.models import PriorConfig becomes from fdia_analysis.models.config import PriorConfig, and likewise models.inputs, models.scores, models.data, models.grid, models.federated, models.training and models.results. The bundles the data dictionary lists for this toolkit are the ones models/scores.py defines, now in that file's order (the same eleven tables, each unchanged).
  • fdia_analysis.formulas exports no name: a formula is imported from formulas.estimation, formulas.federated, formulas.linalg, formulas.measurement, formulas.metrics, formulas.projection or formulas.trust.
  • As for any package, fdia_analysis.se.methods (or any other submodule) is an attribute of its package only once that submodule has been imported.
  • Names only the tests reached are removed (breaking for these names; no behaviour and no stored byte changed). None was named in the docs or used by either toolkit.
  • FdiaGraph.edge_attr_np is gone: ds.edge_attr.numpy() holds the same values.
  • fdia_graph.engine.records.stealthy_state, with_region and is_feasible are gone: they were aliases of the FalseStateMixin methods of the same names, which every caller already used.
  • fdia_graph.schema.ATTR_KEYS and fdia_graph.schema.CURRENT_LAYERS are gone (the tests that compared a file against them build the two sets themselves, from schema.Attr and the four PMU_I* paths).
  • fdia_graph.timeline.DEFAULT_FAMILIES is gone: it was models.choices.GENERATED_FAMILIES.
  • fdia_graph.generation.nygrid.loads.SWITCH_INDUSTRIAL_MW is gone: a constant no code read.
  • A name is imported from the module that defines it: the tables of re-exported names are removed (breaking for these import paths; no behaviour and no stored byte changed). fg.load, fg.generate, the profile helpers, fg.FdiaGraph and the rest of import fdia_graph as fg are unchanged, and so is fdia_graph.timeline.generate_timeline.
  • fdia_graph.models exports no name (__all__ and PUBLIC are gone): from fdia_graph.models import RecordBundle becomes from fdia_graph.models.data import RecordBundle, and likewise models.base (Bundle), models.config (the settings), models.inputs, models.fields, models.frames, models.grid (NODE, EDGE, CURRENT, MeterPlan, ...), models.plan and models.assets. The bundles the data dictionary lists are the ones models/data.py defines.
  • fdia_graph.formulas exports no name: a formula is imported from formulas.network, formulas.noise, formulas.attacks, formulas.temporal or formulas.trust.
  • fdia_graph.generation.nygrid exports no name: nygrid_case, Case and ZONES come from generation.nygrid.case, Network from .network, read_pool and write_pool from .io, Pool, PoolBuilder, peak_ratings and the solve kinds from .pool, NewYorkSource, SingleEpisodeSource and Survey from .source, Settings and rng from .config, and so on by module; Dataset and ClientView from fdia_graph.dataset.clients, ipopt from fdia_graph.engine.solvers.
  • fdia_graph.engine.sensing exports no name (meters.MeterPlan, meters.plan_meters, meters.KINDS, measure.Measurement, noise.NoiseModel), and fdia_graph.engine none: FdiaGenerator is fdia_graph.engine.core.FdiaGenerator.
  • fdia_graph.generation no longer serves DesignPool, IeeeSource and TimelineSource: they are generation.design.DesignPool, generation.ieee.IeeeSource and generation.source.TimelineSource.
  • The module fdia_graph._lazy (attach) is removed with the tables it served.
  • The errors have one home, fdia_graph.errors, which now defines them: the module fdia_graph.models.errors is removed, and ConfigError and MissingCapability are no longer names of fdia_graph.models.validation. The classes are the same ones, so an except clause is unaffected; their __module__ is now fdia_graph.errors, which is what a traceback, a repr and a pickle name.
  • fdia_graph.formulas.<module> and fdia_graph.models.<module> are attributes of the package only once that submodule has been imported, as for any package: import fdia_graph.formulas alone no longer makes fdia_graph.formulas.network reachable; import fdia_graph.formulas.network does.
  • The module-level __all__ lists of models.fields, formulas.trust, engine.solvers, generation.nygrid.tables and fdia_analysis.se.detect.rules are removed. Nothing star-imported these modules; from fdia_graph import * keeps its list.
  • import fdia_graph loads six fewer modules than before (four formula modules, models.frames and models.plan, which only the tables pulled in) and, as before, neither pandapower, torch, pandas, scipy nor Pyomo.
  • One file layout: a New York timeline is written in the layout of every timeline (breaking for New York files; IEEE files are unchanged). The New York grid wrote its own layout with its own writer and reader. It now writes the groups, datasets and attributes named in fdia_graph.schema, through the writer the IEEE cases use (generation/write.py, generation/emit.py), and FdiaGraph opens the file. No number moved: the readings, the benign readings, the tampered meters and the attacked buses gathered back from a new file were compared, bit for bit, with the arrays the old layout stored, on the three digest files (twelve comparisons, all equal; a one-time proof, run before the three New York digests were re-recorded and then removed), and the two IEEE whole-file digests pass unchanged. The three New York digests are re-recorded, since every path in them changed.
  • Old New York files stop reading. There is no converter and no fallback: Dataset refuses a file in the earlier layout with NotATimeline, and fdia-graph 0.21 reads it. Regenerate the file to use it with this version.
  • Paths. frames/z [T, M] is now three layers with their masks, zero where no meter sits: data/node_x [T, N, 4] (|V|, P, Q, angle), data/edge_x [T, E, 4] (P and Q flow at the from end, then at the to end) and data/pmu_i [T, E, 4] (current magnitude and angle at the from end, then at the to end), with data/node_m, data/edge_m, data/pmu_i_m. frames/z_benign is benign/node_benign, benign/edge_benign, benign/pmu_i_benign. labels/meter_tampered is attack/node_tamper, attack/edge_tamper, attack/pmu_i_tamper; labels/bus_attacked is data/y. frames/time, split, family and episode are data/time, data/split, data/family and data/seq_id. frames/vm and frames/va are columns 0 and 3 of clean/node_clean.
  • Family codes. data/family and episodes/family carry the one table of models/choices.py: 7 for Am and 5 for At, where a New York file had 1 for Am and 2 for At (and episodes/family held the names as text). The New York table FAMILIES of generation.nygrid.io and the file attributes family_codes, split_codes and kind_codes are removed.
  • Types. The labels are uint8 (were bool); the true state is float32 in clean/node_clean (vm and va were float64); episodes/onset, length and target_branch are int32 (were int64); the episode buses are episodes/bus_idx (int32) with offsets episodes/bus_ptr (were buses, buses_ptr, int64).
  • Added. clean/node_clean also holds the P and Q injections of the solved state, and clean/edge_clean its exact flows at the metered branch ends. graph/ holds the edge index, the branch model and bus shunts that give the admittance matrix (it equals the case's, tests/nygrid/test_dataset.py), the bus type, voltage limits, base kV, base load and generator flag, and bus_client. The root carries the attributes of every timeline that apply (kind, system, N, E, T, baseMVA, seed, the legends, the split and episode counts, settings and settings_hash) and three of its own: client_names, current_form and the wider edge_feat (P_from,Q_from,P_to,Q_to). Also data/stealthy, data/timestep and the empty attack/mag* tables, as in every timeline.
  • What identifies a file. settings (JSON) and settings_hash record NewYorkSource.record: the settings of the timeline (the new NewYorkSettings.as_record) and, under release, the knobs of the NewYorkRelease the source was built for (families, interfaces, hold_external, v_margin, gen_v_tol, load_cap, band; the new NewYorkRelease.as_record), so two files that differ in a release knob have different hashes. A single-episode file records its episode (episode: family, onset, lag and the pool frames it covers) in place of the attacked share, the splits and the survey; it has no target_attacked_frac, and its split_frac is 1, 0, 0. A family passed as using is not recorded.
  • Line ratings. graph/edge_rating (MVA, New York only) holds the ratings the attacks were designed against. The release rates a branch the case file leaves unrated at its peak flow over the pool (N8), so the case file alone does not give them.
  • The integers of graph/ (edge_index, bus_type, bus_client) are int32 on every platform, the type of an IEEE file's edge_index; they were the platform's own integer (int64 on Linux).
  • Removed. case/ (the unit table, the HVDC links, the names and places of the buses and the base state, which are the case file's, generation/nygrid/case_nygrid.m; the line ratings moved to graph/edge_rating), meters/ (the table is rebuilt from the masks; the accuracy class is the table ACCURACY, the bias is drawn from the seed and is not stored, the owner is the owner of the meter's bus), case/tie_lines (a branch whose ends have two owners) and episodes/clients (the owners of an episode's tampered meters).
  • What a New York file declares differently from an IEEE one. Its flow layers are four wide. Its PMU currents are polar (current_form = "polar"; an IEEE file stores real and imaginary parts and carries no such attribute); the estimators' pseudo-measurements, which read real and imaginary parts, refuse a polar file with MissingCapability (the new capability rectangular_currents). Its labels keep the New York rule, written in the tamper attribute of attack/: a meter is tampered where the attack moves its reading by more than its accuracy-class standard deviation, and a bus is attacked where a meter at it is tampered. It has no data/temporal_delta and no data/swing.
  • FdiaGraph on a New York file. The pandas export has a column per stored flow, so a four-wide file also gives P_to_e{n} and Q_to_e{n} (an IEEE table is unchanged). A units="pu" view gives the angles of polar PMU currents in radians, as it gives theta, in records and exports. An estimator refuses a file whose system is no IEEE case with MissingCapability (it was a KeyError). The refusal of windows() on a view that is not consecutive now names a week split, whose weeks interleave with the other splits'.
  • Code. MeterPlan gains scatter (a value per meter laid out as the layers), from_masks (the table a file's masks describe, in plan_meters row order) and gather (the flat vector read back from the layers). Dataset reads schema paths; it gains z(frames, benign=False) and tampered(frames) and no longer has case or kinds (the kinds are the constant KINDS of engine/sensing/meters.py, and ClientView no longer takes them). TimelineWriter, open_timeline and FAMILIES are removed from fdia_graph.generation.nygrid with no alias; read_pool and write_pool stay. The writer's functions take what both grids have: start_timeline, finish_timeline(f, buf, columns), timeline_attrs(header, buf, knobs, record), placement_attrs(rec, split, ...), and LayerSet (models/frames.py) says which layers a grid's file carries. What every source does when it finishes a file is written once, in TimelineSource (record, the settings a file is identified by, and _finish_file).

  • A New York days file (576 frames) is 4.2 MB, from 2.9 MB: the layers hold a zero where no meter sits and the masks are stored per frame, as in an IEEE file.

  • Two toolkits in one repository (breaking for the imports of the analysis packages). The package was generation and analysis in one; it is now two distributions that live side by side here. fdia-graph (the package fdia_graph, under src/) generates a timeline and loads it. fdia-analysis (the package fdia_analysis, under analysis/, with its own pyproject.toml, tests and README) is what is measured on a timeline. The analysis toolkit depends on the generation toolkit (it reads the files through fdia_graph.dataset and uses its formulas and records); nothing in fdia_graph imports fdia_analysis, which tests/test_toolkit_boundary.py checks in the source and by generating and loading a timeline in an interpreter where fdia_analysis cannot be imported. No generated file changes (the timeline digests of the IEEE cases and of New York are the same, the settings hash stored in a file included) and no result number changes (no results block of the docs changed). No alias is kept for a moved name.

  • What a caller sees, in short. The imports of the analysis packages change from fdia_graph.* to fdia_analysis.* (from fdia_graph.se import WLS becomes from fdia_analysis.se.methods import WLS). The se and federated extras move to fdia-analysis (pip install "fdia-graph[se]" becomes pip install "fdia-analysis[se]"). The two toolkits share one version and are released together: fdia-analysis X.Y.Z requires exactly fdia-graph==X.Y.Z, so upgrading one upgrades the other.
  • What moved, package by package: fdia_graph.se is fdia_analysis.se (with fdia_analysis.se.detect), fdia_graph.localization is fdia_analysis.localization, fdia_graph.federated is fdia_analysis.federated, fdia_graph.trust is fdia_analysis.trust, and fdia_graph.results (the results store's code) is fdia_analysis.results. Their classes and functions keep their names and behaviour: from fdia_analysis.se.methods import WLS, from fdia_analysis.localization.methods import SwingThreshold.
  • What stays in fdia_graph: fg.load, fg.generate, FdiaGraph, the profiles, the registry and the download, the file protocol (schema), generation (the New York grid included), engine, dataset, ratings, errors (every named error, the ones the analysis packages raise too), and the models and formulas the generator or the loader use. import fdia_graph as fg and everything under fg. are unchanged.
  • The models only the analysis packages use are in fdia_analysis.models. The settings (from models.config): SolveConfig, FitOptions, HuberConfig, RemovalConfig, PriorConfig, JacobianWeightingConfig, GateConfig, LocalizerConfig, LearnedConfig, TrainerConfig, PerBusReport, TrustConfig, DqnConfig, FederatedSettings, with the field types Fraction, Share, Norm and Tolerance. The fixed sets (from models.choices): Calibrate, Reweight, Features, FrOver, Buses, Kcl, Reduce. What the analysis formulas accept (from models.inputs): ShapedArray, SubBatch, EdgeList, ClientCount, ClientGraph, Halo, AssignmentSpec, PartitionOnGrid, ClientUpdates, MomentParts, FeatureBlock, Affinity, StateBlocks, LabelGrids, TauSearch, RankedLabels, Aggregation, and the rule IntegerDtype (from models.validation, now beside the models that declare it in fdia_analysis.models.inputs). The score tables (all of models.scores): ErrorPair, EstimatorScores, OverallMetrics, BenignMetrics, FamilyMetrics, LocalizerScores, PerBusMetrics, PerBusScores, GridScores, TrustScores, JacobianOutputs. And TrueState (from models.data), PseudoLinks and PseudoVoltages (from models.grid), Partition and RoundLog (all of models.federated), OptimConfig (all of models.training), and the results store's records (all of models.results: Record, Provenance, RunRecords, Metric, METRICS, Better, Leaf, KEYS, leaves, as_values). Each is in the module of the same name (fdia_analysis.models.config, and so on). The loader's bundles are the ones fdia_graph.models.data defines; the score tables are the ones fdia_analysis.models.scores defines.
  • The formulas only the analysis packages use are in fdia_analysis.formulas. Whole modules: formulas.estimation (normal_matrix, wls_step, wls_step_batched, weighted_objective, residual_covariance_diag, critical_measurements, floored_covariance, normalized_residual, huber_weights, whitened_svd_basis, gate_weights, pmu_pseudo_links, pmu_pseudo_phasors, pmu_pseudo_voltages), formulas.linalg (guarded_inverse, condition_number, batched_normal_matrices), formulas.metrics (perbus_counts, perbus_counts_at, perbus_f1_from_counts, tau_from_counts, perbus_rates, micro_prf, sample_f1, strict_accuracy, average_precision), formulas.projection (bus_incidence, weighted_pseudoinverse, leverage, weak_directions, explained_unexplained, direction_coefficients, weak_move, meters_to_buses, meter_positions) and formulas.federated (Moments, channel_moments, pool_moments, fedavg, attackable_affinity, interior_boundary, cut_edge_count, hop_distance, halo_nodes, block_diagonal_basis). Parts of modules: the estimator's measurement function and its Jacobian, ac_measurement and ac_jacobian, left formulas.network for the new fdia_analysis.formulas.measurement; attack_subspace, sparse_basis, attack_cost and greedy_trusted_meters left formulas.trust for fdia_analysis.formulas.trust, which builds on the rref that stays in fdia_graph.formulas.trust beside sparsest_rows (the attack generator uses both); that module's tolerance is now the public TOL.
  • Three names moved inside fdia_graph, to where the generation code that uses them is. accuracy_class_sigma is in formulas.noise (it was in formulas.estimation; the meter noise model uses it). Ownership and assign_clients, which utility owns which New York bus, are in generation.nygrid.ownership (the module was federated.utilities). config_hash, the hash of the settings a timeline stores (settings_hash), is in schema (it was in results.run, which now imports it); the hash of a given settings record is the same.
  • Install: pip install fdia-graph for the loader, with [torch], [pyg], [generate], [iso], [ny] and [all] as before; pip install fdia-analysis for the analysis toolkit, which installs fdia-graph, with the extras [se] (pandapower, scipy), [torch], [federated] (torch, scikit-learn) and [all]. The [se] and [federated] extras of fdia-graph are gone, and its [all] no longer brings scikit-learn; the install hints in the analysis toolkit's error messages name fdia-analysis.

  • In the repository: each toolkit has its tests (tests/, analysis/tests/), which share the tiny generated timeline through the fixtures of the root conftest.py and the helpers of tests/helpers.py; pytest at the root runs both on this checkout's source. tools/prereview.py is still the one command for every gate, now over both packages (tools/sources.py names them once for every tool), the file map and the data dictionary list both, the module diagram draws both with every arrow between them pointing from analysis to generation, and tools/layout.py resolves a cited name in the toolkit it says (fdia_analysis.se.base) or, with none said, in either. CI installs both and tests both; publish.yml (which runs on a version tag only) builds both distributions and uploads both, since they share the tag's version (tests/test_versions.py, and tools/release.py before it tags).

  • One path generates a timeline, for the IEEE cases and for the New York grid (breaking for the New York build's callers). TimelineSource.generate(out) (generation/source.py) makes every timeline in the same order: start the file, prepare, cut the splits, then split by split place the episodes (generation/plan.py), design them and walk the frames in time order, then finish the file. The New York grid no longer has a driver of its own. No generated value changes: the five pinned timelines (two IEEE-14, the New York days, two single episodes) are the same, dataset by dataset, and their snapshots were not rewritten.

  • The grid is a class hierarchy. TimelineSource is the system a timeline is generated on, and a subclass owns only what differs between the grids: the pool, what it must know before the splits (prepare), how the splits are cut (cut_splits), which onsets a family may take (onset_masks), the stream the onsets are drawn from (placement_rng), how an episode is designed and what happens when no design exists (design), how the frames are emitted (walk(until)) and the file layout (open, finish, close). The subclasses are IeeeSource (generation/ieee.py: blocks in time order, no mask, an Am with no design is moved), NewYorkSource (generation/nygrid/source.py: whole weeks, the families' masks and the onset survey, an episode with no design is left benign) and, under it, SingleEpisodeSource (one episode placed by hand). The placement itself is one function for both, place_split. The two file layouts are unchanged.
  • What a caller of the New York build now calls: NewYorkSource.production(pool_path, NewYorkRelease(...)).generate(path), then source.summary() for what was placed and built. The arguments production_builder took are the fields of NewYorkRelease (models/config.py: families, interfaces, workers, survey, survey_cache, root, hold_external, v_margin, gen_v_tol, load_cap, band), checked when it is built; the build Settings (the seed) is the third argument. One episode alone: SingleEpisodeSource(source, onset, family, lo, hi, using=..., lag=...).generate(path), then its summary(). pipelines/newyork/build_timeline.py and build_single_episodes.py do exactly that.
  • NewYorkSource(pool, attacker, families, own, settings, build) takes the timeline's settings as a NewYorkSettings (length, attacked_frac, split, split_by, workers, block, verbose, survey, survey_cache); the measurement is the attacker's and the noise model is made from its meter plan. AttackFamily.onset_mask is part of the family interface (None by default: the family may start anywhere).
  • Removed, with no alias: TimelineBuilder and its module generation/nygrid/timeline.py (its build, build_episode, _slots, _designs, _write and its worker pool), production_builder, TimelineBuilder.episode_lengths (now NewYorkSource.lengths), and the module generation/nygrid/build.py: fetch_inputs and the pinned URLs are in generation/nygrid/inputs.py. timeline.py no longer holds the IEEE set-up (_generator, _knobs, _recorded, _write): it is in IeeeSource.
  • fg.generate and generate_timeline("ieee14", ...) are unchanged: generate_timeline is IeeeSource(system, states, settings, seed).generate(out). An IeeeSource generates one timeline (its generator's random stream is used up); a second generate is a ConfigError.
  • Behaviour that changed:
    • A failed run leaves no file, on either grid. A timeline is written beside out as <out>.part and takes the name out only when it is whole. Before, the file was created at the start of the run: a rerun destroyed the file already there at once, and a run that failed left a stub that opened as a timeline.
    • Design workers are spawned on every OS (generation.design.DesignPool, one pool for both grids, started once per timeline). A script that passes workers above 1 must start under if __name__ == "__main__":, on Linux too (before, IEEE workers were forked there). After a failed run the workers are stopped at once instead of finishing the designs in flight. A single episode is designed in the caller's process.
    • New York frames are written in stretches, each as soon as every week before it is planned, instead of one pass after every design. The noise stream still runs over the frames in time order, so no value depends on where a stretch or a block ends; tests/nygrid/test_stretches.py pins that against a one-pass build on a synthetic pool, with no data and no solver.
    • NewYorkSource.generate() with no path is a ConfigError (the IEEE default path is unchanged).
    • The warning for an episode dropped by a jammed placement reads the same on both grids: "split train: placements jammed 10 times, 1 Am episode(s) dropped" (the New York one did not give the count of tries).
    • A single episode with no attack still raises NoAdmissibleTarget, now from generate; an unsolved window or a window outside the file's frames is refused when the SingleEpisodeSource is built.
    • The release build asks for each unit's output in the pool (unit_p) only when it builds Am.
  • Records (models/plan.py): SplitSpan may list its frames (a split of whole weeks) and says where an episode fits (onsets_fit); Designed and Placement serve both grids' families; Schedule.lengths. place_split(rng, lengths, frac, span, rec, masks) takes the lengths and the fraction instead of a Schedule; AmDesigner.design_split returns the split's episodes as Designed records and walk_split takes them; planned_until says how far the walk may run once a split is planned.

  • An AC operator (New York grid). OperatorPolicy(dispatch="ac") and dispatch="ac_cost" run the operator's dispatch as an AC optimal power flow each scan (AcSced, Pyomo and Ipopt, OperatorOpf): the loads it reads (the true loads plus what the attack changed in its New York injection meters; the accounting operator adds the false interchange back over New York's loads by their size), the units within the pool's own bounds (PoolFrames, pool_frames, PoolBuilder.frame_limits) and their five-minute ramps from its previous dispatch, hydro and external units under the pool's anchor, bus voltage and reactive limits, the four interfaces' AC flows within their limits, and the shed, shortage and balance prices of DcSced. ac moves the least generation; ac_cost clears at least cost and prices every bus at its AC balance dual (Twin.price). Its benign twin stays at the AC points (both solve the pool's problem). The closed loop re-solves on what the operator reads after its own dispatch (true AC flows less its AC model), not on shift factors, the N-1 screen is an AC power flow per outage (TrueGrid(day, ac=True), ac_power_flow), shedding and the zone levers use AC sensitivities (ac_shift). The DC dispatches and their results are unchanged.

  • A least-cost dispatch that keeps the AC operating points (New York grid). DcSced(objective="cost_lf") and OperatorPolicy(dispatch="cost_lf") (--dispatch cost_lf on every study tool) run the market dispatch around the AC operating point, as an RTO's incremental dispatch is: each unit's cost counts per MW delivered to the reference bus (loss_factors, the power flow Jacobian's delivery factors at the frame's true AC state), the balance is written on the delivered change, the first scan ramps from the basepoint, offline quick-start units start only when the committed units leave a constraint unmet, and the AC point's implied values (DcSced.implied: the least bus and unit adders that make the AC point this model's least-cost dispatch) carry what the AC dispatch priced and the DC model does not see. The plain least-cost dispatch moves its benign twin 1.2 to 4.1 GW off the AC points on at-limit days; this one keeps it there. Each run now reports every bus's price (Twin.price, DcSced.prices), and area_damage's payments use it. The movement and cost dispatches are unchanged.

PoolBuilder applies its limits and records each bank's output (shunt_q), which enters the power flow and the pool's injections. Without a Compensation the model, the pool and every released file are unchanged.

The least-cost dispatch holds a binding interface at its shift-factor limit, so its true flow can pass the limit with no attack, which the old counts charged to the attack. benign_margin_min_mw reports the benign twin's tightest margin. Operator is the protocol a partner's operator implements (return a Response and summarize works on it), and NyisoOperator(policy) is this package's.

  • The operator in one module per job (New York grid). fdia_graph.nyfed.operator.response (730 lines) is split into day (reading an attacked day), ties (the interchange check), truegrid (the AC power flows on the true grid), policy (the operator's choices), run (the scan-by-scan loop) and summary (its consequence), the code moved as it was. response re-exports every name, so existing imports keep working. The interchange check's alarm is public as interchange_alarm.

  • Detection as building blocks (New York grid). New fdia_graph.nyfed.detect: the residual test's AC weighted least squares (wls, returning a WlsFit that says whether it converged), the noise-free fit of a state (exact_state), the persistence rule with its calibration (PersistenceRule, PersistenceRule.fit) behind an AlarmRule protocol any other rule can implement, and other meter fleets (with_fleet, fleet_bias). TrueGrid.state and TrueGrid.run_state give the true state after the operator acts, with the load it shed (the research tools left the shed load out; no studied day sheds load, so no number changes). The six detection tools under pipelines/newyork/ now drive these instead of carrying their own copies and importing each other.

  • Settings are arguments, not patches (New York grid). production_builder takes v_margin and gen_v_tol, the attacker's voltage sensitivities (N71, N75); v_margin widens the limits on the attacker's own copy of the case (Case.with_voltage_margin). Before, the damage study widened the shared case's arrays in place, so a timeline written from that builder recorded the widened limits. InterfaceFdia.with_overshoot returns a variant as a copy, and max_overshoot searches on one, instead of swapping overshoot in and out; build_episode(using=...) designs with such a variant. hourly_dispatch(hold_externals=False) replaces the AC ablation's monkeypatch.

  • A public surface for the New York grid. Every fdia_graph.nyfed package (grid, scenario, sensing, attacks, timeline, operator, and fdia_graph.nyfed itself) now has a docstring that says what its stage does, what goes in and comes out, and how it fails, and an __all__ of its public names, loaded on first use (reading a dataset still never imports pandapower or Pyomo). Helpers the research tools reached into became public: operator.response.TrueGrid and entry_share (the old private names _TrueGrid and _entry_share are gone), Attacker.absorb and TimelineBuilder.episode_lengths.

Both subclass ValueError, so existing handlers keep working. The input CSV tables are read through one reader that closes them (fdia_graph.nyfed.tables), and the research tools no longer silence warnings. docs/guides/troubleshooting_new_york.md lists what each stage reports when it fails and what to do.

  • A failed power flow reads as unknown, not safe (New York grid). The operator's Twin gains pf_failed [T], the scans whose AC power flow on the true grid failed, and summarize reports pf_failed_scans and pf_failed_benign_scans. Before, those scans' NaN margins counted as within the limit with no trace. respond now rejects an unknown after (before, a typo ran as an operator that never answers the alarm), and an unknown mode, after or entry raises fdia_graph.errors.ConfigError (a ValueError, as before).

AttackFamily.design_explained returns the episode or the reason there is none (one of fdia_graph.nyfed.attacks.episode.MISSES: no_target, infeasible, solver_error), also kept in last_miss, and TimelineBuilder.build reports missed and, with the onset survey, survey_missed: the count of each reason per family. build_episode's error names the reason. Before, a timeline with few attacks gave no way to tell an empty window from a failing solver.

  • A missing solver now says so (New York grid). fdia_graph.nyfed.solvers.ipopt finds Ipopt in the environment, checks that it starts, and raises the new fdia_graph.errors.SolverUnavailable with the fix when it does not. Before, an Ipopt that could not start (a missing DLL, exit code 0xC0000135) made every attack design read as infeasible, so a timeline built with no overload attacks and no error. The attack OPF now reads only an abnormal stop on its own model as an infeasible support, and counts those in solver_errors.

  • Answering a residual alarm (New York grid). respond(after=...) models the operator's response to an alarm (switch to the benign scans, freeze with the AGC on the falsified ties, freeze with it on the common source) (N78).

  • The residual test with the meters' noise (New York grid). respond(alarm_at=...) models an operator that falls back at the first residual alarm (N77).

  • The closed loop (New York grid). respond(closed_loop=True) has the operator read the true flows after its dispatch (N76).

  • Voltage checks and the overload record (New York grid). production_builder(gen_v_tol=...) holds generator voltages near their schedule (N75), and summarize reports how long an interface stays past its true limit.

  • Entry patterns and many meter fleets (New York grid). respond(entry=...) chooses where the inadvertent interchange enters (N72).

  • Where the inadvertent interchange lands, and the certificate's reach (New York grid). The shortfall the trusting operator leaves is now taken up by the synchronous units outside New York in proportion to their capacity rather than by the reference bus, and every scan reports the tightest true interface margin (margin, summary margin_min_mw and margin_lost_mw) (N69). production_builder(v_margin=...) widens the attacker's voltage limits (N71). A failed power flow now leaves the margin unknown.

  • Three operators and a calibrated interchange check (New York grid). respond(mode=...) runs the trusting operator, whose AGC reads the falsified New York-end tie meters, the accounting operator, which takes its load and ACE from the agreed interchange (BAL-005), and the oracle upper bound (N66; replaces defended). The neighbours' tie meters carry their own accuracy-class noise (neighbour_reads); respond(calib=...) takes the alarm's calibration (N67). The consistent attacker's area stays inside New York. The target interface comes first, the shed clock runs per interface, and the oracle falls back at decision time.

  • The interchange-consistent attacker and the interchange check (New York grid). Attacker(hold_external=True) (and production_builder(..., hold_external=True)) keeps every bus outside New York at its true injection, so the attack cannot move New York's net interchange (N62). The operator gets the matching check, tie_gap: the interchange read at the New York ends of the ties less what the neighbours meter. respond(..., defended=True) stops acting on the tampered scans from the first alarm (N65). The operator now enforces all four mapped interfaces, each with its own 15-minute clock and shortage price. It may start the quick-start units of zones J and K, and it caps regulation at 275 MW, reporting the rest as an ACE excursion (N63, N64). Shed load takes its reactive demand with it, and a reused day keeps its meter count.

  • The damaging attack and the operator's escalation (New York grid). InterfaceFdia(overshoot=...) takes the reported interface flow past its limit, designed under every bound as a real attack, and max_overshoot finds the largest overshoot an onset allows by bisection (N58). The operator now escalates as NYISO's emergency procedures do (N59): redispatch first, the flow it cannot relieve priced at the 2019 transmission shortage curve (shortage_usd, N60), and load relief after 15 minutes over the limit at the buses where shedding relieves the interface. Step carries the shed load and the cost of relieving the interface.

  • The grid operator under attack (fdia_graph.nyfed.operator). DcSced is the operator's real-time dispatch on what it sees: a DC dispatch on shift factors around the pool basepoint, with unit limits, five-minute ramps from its previous dispatch and the interface limit (the benign model flow plus the hour's real 2019 headroom). It moves as little as it must, then at least cost. respond(day, delay, over) runs it on a day's attacked scans and on their benign twin, in closed loop on the dispatch. The true load never changed, so regulation picks up the generation the dispatch removed, and an AC power flow gives the true interface flow and the worst single 345 kV outage. summarize reports the attack's consequence, attacked less benign: dispatch moved, regulation (MW, MWh, by utility), unrelieved flow, the true interface and N-1 changes, production cost and the energy settled at the real zonal LBMP (N50 to N57).

  • [WU26]'s own attack construction as the overload attack's support method (OverloadSettings.support_method, "search" by default or "rref"; new choice SupportMethod, FrameKnobs.support_method, file attribute support_method). CsvColumn checks its path and column when built (a missing column used to surface as a pandas KeyError on read), and a dataset name that is neither a name nor a bus count, such as fg.load(["ieee14"]), is a ConfigError instead of a raw TypeError. A profile date span that ends before it starts, and an IsoFolder directory that is not a path, are refused when given; generate(states=pathlib.Path(...)) now reads the file instead of failing with an AttributeError. Arguments reach their models unconverted, so a malformed one is a ConfigError, not the raw error of a conversion done first: families=3, pool_moments(None), fedavg(None, ...), block_diagonal_basis(3, d), score(ds, scores="bad"), score(ds, xhat="bad") and a non-numeric in-memory state pool. A test refuses Model(tuple(arg))-style calls in the package. A Huber c, a removal threshold, am_rate and the learned localizer's lr and pos_weight must be finite as well as positive, and a solver tol finite and non-negative. The learned localizer checks its whole training setup (dropout, lr, weight_decay, batch_size, epochs, pos_weight, seed) on LearnedConfig when it is built. generate_timeline checks families on FamilySelection before it builds the case, and the admissible-target check is a model, models.inputs.AdmissibleTargets, which raises NoAdmissibleTarget as before (a model names its failure type in Validated.error; the named data errors now live in models.errors and fdia_graph.errors re-exports them). TimelineKnobs.am_len defaults to None, resolved to ramp_len by the model. check_partition is deprecated in favour of building PartitionOnGrid, and the internal check_window_args and check_targets are gone (WindowSpec, AdmissibleTargets). A value no model can even read (a number past the float range, a mapping where a sequence belongs) is a ConfigError, never a raw OverflowError, KeyError or AttributeError; tests/test_malformed_inputs.py sweeps every config and input model with values of the wrong kind and the public entry points with one bad argument each. Loose input is read by a parser model, so no function outside models/ dispatches on a type: ProfileSource (what load_profile was handed), DateSpan (fetch_profile's dates; a date it cannot read is a ConfigError before any download), StateSource (an in-memory pool or a path) and DatasetName (the registry's lookup key). tools/readability.py now refuses isinstance(...) outside fdia_graph.models as it refuses a bare raise ValueError.
  • The estimator solve path no longer takes the slack angle. _solve(z, w), _w_solve(z, w), _nres(x, z) and the rest solve at the fitted reference (ref_angles, through the new _h_ref(x)); a custom SEBase subclass that overrides _solve drops its thsl argument. JacobianFeatures.previous_estimate returns the state alone. The numbers are unchanged.
  • Detectors calibrate from measurements only. SEBase.fit(ds, calibrate="measured") sets every meter's sigma from its accuracy class (formulas.estimation.accuracy_class_sigma, the classes now one definition, engine.base.ACCURACY_CLASS, shared with the noise model), takes the angle reference from the case and the linearization point from the mean estimate of the benign training scans, and reads no clean layer. The Jacobian feature sets, ResidualLocalizer and TrustSelector fit their estimator this way; the state estimators keep calibrate="truth" as the benchmark default. Residual-based sigmas were tried first and rejected: a meter's constant bias is absorbed into the state, so they shrink on the biased meters and collapse the fit. The frozen localization reference moves for the residual arm.
