docs.title: The timeline file
docs.text:
A New York timeline has the layout of every timeline: the groups, datasets and attributes named in fdia_graph.schema, written by the writer the IEEE cases use and read by FdiaGraph and by Dataset. The meters are a flat table (MeterPlan, [M] rows) in the code and layers in the file. MeterPlan.scatter puts one value per meter at its place in the layers; MeterPlan.from_masks rebuilds the table from the file's meter masks, in the same row order; MeterPlan.gather reads the flat vector back, so Dataset.z(frames) is bit for bit the vector the file was written from, and a client's data is still z[:, meters.owner == c].

group dataset shape data/ node_x (observed |V| p.u., P MW, Q MVAr, angle deg), mask node_m, float32, zero where no meter [T, N, 4] data/ edge_x (observed P and Q flow at the from end, then at the to end), mask edge_m [T, E, 4] data/ pmu_i (PMU current magnitude p.u. and angle deg at the from end, then at the to end), mask pmu_i_m [T, E, 4] data/ y (uint8, 1 at an attacked bus), family (int8: 0 benign, 5 At, 7 Am), stealthy, seq_id (int32 episode row, -1 benign), timestep, split (int8: 0 train, 1 val, 2 test), time (int64 s, NYISO's local clock) [T, N], [T] benign/ node_benign, edge_benign, pmu_i_benign: the same scans without the attack as data/ clean/ node_clean (the true state |V|, P, Q, angle, float32), edge_clean (the exact flows at the metered branch ends) [T, N, 4], [T, E, 4] attack/ node_tamper, edge_tamper, pmu_i_tamper (uint8, 1 at a tampered meter); mag_ptr, mag_bus, mag (empty: the attack is observed minus benign) as data/ graph/ edge_index, the branch model and bus shunts that give the admittance matrix (edge_r, edge_x, edge_b, edge_g, edge_gs, edge_bs, edge_tap, edge_shift, edge_status, edge_is_trafo, bus_shunt_g, bus_shunt_b), edge_rating (MVA, the line ratings the attacks were designed against), bus_type, bus_vmin, bus_vmax, bus_base_kv, bus_has_gen, bus_base_pd, bus_base_qd, and bus_client (the utility that owns each bus, -1 outside New York) [E], [N] episodes/ one row per Episode: family (the same codes), onset, length, target_branch; the ragged buses as bus_idx with [S + 1] offsets bus_ptr [S]

What reads differently from an IEEE file is declared in the file itself:

  • The flow layers are four wide, both branch ends (the attribute edge_feat is P_from,Q_from,P_to,Q_to); an IEEE file meters the from end only.
  • The PMU currents are magnitude and angle (the attribute current_form is polar); an IEEE file stores real and imaginary parts. Code that reads a current as real and imaginary parts refuses a polar file (MissingCapability), as the pseudo-measurements of the estimators do.
  • The labels follow this grid's rule (the attribute tamper of attack/): a meter is tampered where the attack moves its reading by more than its accuracy-class standard deviation, and a bus is attacked where a meter at it is tampered.
  • The temporal layers (temporal_delta, swing) are left out; ClientView.temporal() computes each client's from its own z.
  • client_names (root attribute) names the utilities in the order graph/bus_client indexes.

The root attributes are those of every timeline that apply: kind, system, N, E, T, baseMVA, seed, the feature legends, families, attacked_frac, n_episodes, the split sizes and the episodes requested and built per split and family, and settings with settings_hash: what identifies the file, as JSON (NewYorkSource.record: the settings of the timeline and, under release, the knobs of the NewYorkRelease it was built for). A single-episode file records its one episode there (episode: family, onset, lag and the pool frames it covers) in place of the attacked share, the splits and the survey, and carries no target_attacked_frac.

Not in the file: the unit table, the HVDC links and the bus names and places, which are the case file's (generation/nygrid/case_nygrid.m). The line ratings are in the file because the case file does not give them all: the release rates a branch the case leaves unrated at its peak flow over the pool (N8), so graph/edge_rating is the ratings the attacks were designed against. Also not in the file: each meter's accuracy class (the table ACCURACY of engine/sensing/meters.py) and its bias (drawn from the seed), and each meter's owner (the owner of its bus).

z - z_benign is the attack. Unsolved pool frames keep their place with NaN state and readings and no labels.

docs.title: The New York grid: one run, end to end
docs.text:
This page follows one attack through every stage of fdia_graph.generation.nygrid, from the network to the clients' view, with the call that does each step. The architecture says how the modules fit together, the troubleshooting page what each stage reports when it fails, and the extending guide how to add an attack or an alarm rule of your own.

The snippets run from a work folder that holds the inputs (python pipelines/newyork/build_timeline.py --fetch, see the guide) and the 2019 pool (pipelines/newyork/run_pool.py, several hours).

docs.title: 1. The network and the clients
docs.text:
The grid is one MATPOWER case file shipped with the package (NYgrid's case with the changes that make it solvable in AC). nygrid_case() reads it into a Case, a frozen record of arrays, and Network holds its admittances. Each New York bus belongs to one utility, a client of the federated dataset.

from fdia_graph.generation.nygrid.case import nygrid_case
from fdia_graph.generation.nygrid.network import Network

case = nygrid_case()
net = Network(case)

A change to the grid is an edit to the case file (the architecture lists its fields); a variant in code is a copy (hvdc_links(case), case.with_voltage_margin(0.02)), never a change in place.

docs.title: 2. The operating points
docs.text:
scenario gives the true AC state of every five-minute frame of 2019: the loads by bus (LoadModel), NYgrid's hourly dispatch, and a ramp-limited least-cost AC dispatch solved frame by frame (PoolBuilder). The year takes hours, so it is built once and read back:

from fdia_graph.generation.nygrid.io import read_pool
from fdia_graph.generation.nygrid.pool import SOLVED

pool = read_pool("out/pool_2019_v3.h5")
print((pool.solve_kind == SOLVED).mean())  # 0.998: the frames that solved; only these are used downstream

docs.title: 3. The meters, the attacker and the timeline
docs.text:
NewYorkSource.production assembles the release's source: the clients, the meter plan, the attacker and its families, over the pool. A source's generate(path) writes its timeline, by the same path the IEEE timelines take. One attack window can be written on its own, which is how the studies of the paper are made:

from fdia_graph.generation.nygrid.source import NewYorkSource, SingleEpisodeSource
from fdia_graph.models.config import NewYorkRelease

release = NewYorkRelease(families=("Am",), workers=1, survey=0)
source = NewYorkSource.production("out/pool_2019_v3.h5", release)
one = SingleEpisodeSource(source, onset=48220, family="Am")  # the interface attack at the limit, on its day
one.generate("one.h5")

The Am family (InterfaceFdia) raises the reported flow of the Sprain Brook and Dunwoodie South interface to its limit while keeping every reading consistent with a false state, so the operator's residual test cannot see it. source.generate(path) writes the whole year instead, with episodes placed at random; source.summary() then counts what it placed, built and, by reason, missed.

docs.title: 4. The clients' view
docs.text:
A client reads only its own meters, and the labels of its own buses:

from fdia_graph.dataset.clients import Dataset

ds = Dataset("one.h5")
view = ds.client(ds.clients[0])
print(view.z.shape, view.labels.shape)  # scans x this client's meters, scans x its buses
every = view.frames  # all frames of the file
attack = ds.z(every) - ds.z(every, benign=True)  # scans x every meter: the attack vector

docs.title: The New York grid: extending it
docs.text: fdia_graph.generation.nygrid is built to take new parts without changes to its own code. This page names each extension point, what it must provide, and a runnable example that implements it. The examples under examples/nygrid/ need no data, and CI runs each of them, so they stay current with the code. For how the stages fit together see the architecture, for one run end to end the walkthrough.

docs.title: What you can add
docs.text: You add It provides It plugs into Example An attack family design(window, rng) -> Episode \| None (subclass AttackFamily) NewYorkSource beside the package's families (source.generate(path) then places, designs and writes its episodes like theirs); onset_mask holds it to the onsets it may take; design_explained reports why a window has none custom_attack_family.py An alarm rule first_alarm(stat) -> int (the AlarmRule protocol) your own detector, in place of PersistenceRule: the package ships the rule and the protocol, and the code that computes the statistic and asks the rule is yours custom_alarm_rule.py

docs.title: An attack family
docs.text:
A family receives a window of true states, (onset, vm [L, N], va [L, N]), and returns an Episode: the attack vector a [L, M] added to each scan, the buses it attacks (the localization labels) and the owners of the meters it moves. Return None where the window holds nothing to attack, and set self.last_miss = "no_target" when that is why; design_explained then reports no_target, and a None left unexplained reads as infeasible.

An attack the operator's residual test should not see has to change the readings as h(x_false) - h(x_true) for a false state, as the package's Attacker does. A family that does not, like the example's slow bias, is the naive attack the residual test is meant to catch, and is useful as a baseline.

docs.title: An alarm rule
docs.text: A rule turns a statistic per scan (a residual sum, a gap between two meters, any score) into the first scan it alarms on, or -1. Calibrate it on benign days only: PersistenceRule.fit takes a percentile of benign statistics, and a rule fitted on no statistic at all is an error (NoBenignRecords), since it would never alarm. Report its false alarms on benign days of other months beside its detection rate.

docs.title: Changing the package itself
docs.text:
• The grid is the MATPOWER case file src/fdia_graph/generation/nygrid/case_nygrid.m, read by nygrid_case(). To change a line, a unit or a limit, edit the file; code does not patch the case on the way in. Edit rows in place, or add and delete whole rows: Case.from_matpower reads the file with matpowercaseframes and refuses a file whose parts disagree, naming the file and what is wrong (the architecture lists the checks). A study on another grid passes its own Case (Case.from_matpower of its own file) wherever the package takes one; that file must follow this file's conventions: area 1 on every bus, and the zone codes of the legend in its header (1 to 11 the NYISO load zones, 12 to 15 the neighbors). A change to the file moves generated numbers, so it comes with the goldens and digests below.
  • The golden snapshots (tests/nygrid/test_golden.py, and analysis/tests/test_detect.py for the persistence rule) pin what the persistence rule and the interface attack return on fixed inputs. A change that should not move a number must pass them unchanged; one that should must rewrite them (NYGRID_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1) and say in the pull request which numbers moved and why.
  • The timeline digests (tests/nygrid/test_timeline_digests.py) pin every dataset and attribute of a built timeline and of two episodes the same way; they are rewritten with FDIA_UPDATE_DIGESTS=1.
  • A setting is an argument; never change a library object's settings or a shared record's arrays after it is built.
  • Raise the named errors of fdia_graph.errors: ConfigError for a wrong argument, a DataConditionError for data that does not meet a condition, SolverUnavailable for an environment that cannot run the solver.
  • A new module is listed in the architecture in the same change. A new public name is imported from its defining module: a package's __init__.py holds no table of names.

docs.title: How a timeline is generated
docs.text:
One timeline per system is the dataset. This page follows it from the load profile to the file, and states which layers a detector may read. Every value below is the code's default; the source of each is named beside it. Terms are defined in ../reference/GLOSSARY.md.

stage code output 1. operating-point pool profiles.fetch_profile, profiles.generate_states, the v0.7.1 pool build [T, N, 4] AC states, one per minute 2. meter plan and noise engine/core.py (FdiaGenerator.__init__), engine/measurement.py which channels are metered, one noisy scan per state 3. attack families engine/attacks/ (the AttackMixin: the false states, the fewest-tamper search and each family's episode design are methods of the generator), engine/records.py the attacked scan of each family 4. plan: split and episode placement generation/plan.py (split_bounds, place_split, planned_until) the split, onsets, lengths 5. design: the overload Am of each split generation/design.py (AmDesigner, in parallel over workers processes) each Am's design, or its move 6. emit and write: the per-frame layers generation/emit.py (Walk.walk_split), generation/write.py (TimelineWriter) the HDF5 file

TimelineSource.generate (generation/source.py) runs stages 4 to 6, for the IEEE cases and for the New York grid alike; each stage hands the next a typed value (the splits, the slots, the designed episodes). The steps that depend on the grid are the methods of the source's subclasses, described next.

docs.title: One path, two grids
docs.text:
A timeline is generated in the same order on either grid, by one method: TimelineSource.generate(out). Its body is short; read it there. In words:

  1. open: the file is started beside out under a .part name. It takes the name out only when it is whole, so a run that fails leaves no file, and a file already at out is left as it was.
  2. prepare: the source works out what it must know before the splits are cut. Nothing on an IEEE case; on the New York grid, the onsets its families may take (their masks, and the onset survey).
  3. cut_splits: train, val and test.
  4. Then, split by split:
  5. place: the split's episodes at uniform random onsets (generation/plan.py, the same code for both grids);
  6. design: what each episode attacks, kept on the source for the walk;
  7. walk: every frame not yet written whose split is planned by now, in time order.
  8. finish: what the file carries besides its frames. Then close, after a failed run too.

A TimelineSource is the grid a timeline is generated on. Each subclass owns only what differs between the grids:

step IeeeSource (generation/ieee.py) NewYorkSource (generation/nygrid/source.py) the pool [T, N, 4] AC states of a pandapower case the year of five-minute AC states (Pool) prepare nothing each waiting family's onset mask; with survey, the onset survey (kept in a Survey record) cut_splits three blocks in time order (split_bounds) whole weeks, stratified (split_weeks) onset_masks none: any onset of the split the masks, or the onsets the survey found an attack at placement_rng the generator's one stream the build's place stream design the overload Am, before the split is walked; one with no design is moved every family; one with no design is left benign walk(until) the frames of the split just designed (its end is until), a scan per frame; a ramp At is designed as the walk reaches it the frames up to until: the noisy benign scan plus the episode's attack vector open, finish the file layout of this page, through generation/write.py the same layout through the same writer, a value per meter laid out as layers (MeterPlan.scatter); what a New York file declares differently is in new_york_grid.md

The walk writes every frame whose split is planned by now (generation.plan.planned_until), and that one rule serves both grids. An IEEE timeline's splits are blocks in time order, so it is the split just designed; and each split is placed only after the one before it is walked, because placements, ramp designs and the moves of an infeasible ramp draw from the generator's one random stream. The New York splits are whole weeks, which interleave in time, so the walk waits until every week before a frame is planned and the file is written in a few stretches. Its noise stream runs over the frames in time order, so the scans do not depend on where a stretch ends (tests/nygrid/test_stretches.py pins that).

SingleEpisodeSource, under NewYorkSource, is the New York grid with one episode placed by hand. The design processes of both grids are one class, generation.design.DesignPool; they are spawned, so a script that asks for more than one worker starts under if __name__ == "__main__":.

generate_timeline("ieee14", ...) is IeeeSource(...).generate(out); the New York build is NewYorkSource.production(pool_path).generate(path). To switch a grid's load profiles, attacks or solver, change what its source holds (the pool, the families); the path stays.

The published default release is v0.8.3 (registry._RELEASE), built by fdia-graph 0.20 with the seven families of that release (the single-snapshot Aq, Al, Ad, As, Ar among them) and the v0.8.3 meters. This version reads every release and generates the multi-snapshot families At and Am on the hybrid meters, the recipe of the next data release. Releases up to v0.8.1 also hold Aq for 15 to 44 frames and Al for 10 to 29, and compute the swing scale from the noiseless pool.

docs.title: 1. Operating-point pools
docs.text:
item value source load profile NYISO system load, 11 zones summed, native 5-minute cadence profiles.NyisoArchive (the NYISO entry of profiles._FEEDS) window 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-16 the v0.7.1 pool build (a release script kept outside the repository; WINDOW) resampling time-interpolated to a 1-minute grid, then standardized to zero mean and unit variance profiles.fetch_profile(resample_min=1) per-bus scale clip(1 + k * S_t + j_t, 0.7, 1.3), k = 0.1 profiles._ar1_scale, K_DEFAULT, CLIP_DEFAULT jitter j_t per-bus AR(1), j_t = 0.98 j_{t-1} + sqrt(1 - 0.98^2) * 0.03 * eps, stationary std 0.03 JITTER_RHO, SIGMA_DEFAULT what is scaled every load's P and Q and every generator's P at the bus, by the same factor profiles._solve_states_chunk solve pandapower AC power flow, flat start, 50 iterations, 1e-6 MVA tolerance profiles._solve_states_chunk states kept 82,000 requested, the first 72,000 converged kept per system the v0.7.1 pool build (REQUEST, TARGET) column order |V| pu, P_inj MW, Q_inj MVAr, theta deg, voltage first generation.as_v_first, pool attribute columns file pool_ieee{C}.h5, dataset X registry.pool_spec

The AR(1) jitter makes each bus drift smoothly from minute to minute rather than jump. The clip holds every bus inside a plausible load band. Shunt draws are subtracted from the stored injections, because the estimator models a shunt in the admittance matrix, not as an injection (profiles._remove_shunt_injections).

Consecutive pool timesteps are one minute apart on the profile grid. A timestep whose power flow does not converge is skipped, not filled, and the pool stores no timestamps. Frame t of a timeline is pool timestep t (data/timestep).

docs.title: 2. Meter plan and noise
docs.text:
The meter plan is drawn once per generator from the seed and is the same on every frame (FdiaGenerator._meter_plan, emit_from_state).

channel metered at default |V| the union of the voltage buses and the PMU buses vbus_frac = 0.6 (int(0.6 N) buses), pmu_frac = 0.2 (max(1, int(0.2 N)) buses) theta the PMU buses (hybrid meters); every |V| bus (v0.8.3 meters) as above branch current, pmu_i both ends' real and imaginary part of every in-service branch with a PMU at that end (hybrid meters only) as above P_inj, Q_inj every injection bus and every zero-injection bus always P_from, Q_from each branch independently with probability flow_frac flow_frac = 0.9

The meter model decides what a meter reads (meter_model in the meter plan, D10 of the attack-design plan, "the plan" on this page: git show 91c15ad:docs/plans/WU_MSFDIA_PLAN.md). The default, "hybrid", is a SCADA and PMU plan as in [WU26]: a SCADA voltmeter reads |V| only, a PMU reads |V|, the angle and the current phasor of every in-service branch at its bus [WU26, eqs. 17-20]. The released files up to v0.8.3 wrote an angle at every voltmeter bus and read no currents; the loader reads them, the generator no longer writes them (models.config.MeterSettings, the plan's D12).

Injection buses are those with a generator, a load, the external grid, a shunt or a producing static generator; every other bus is zero-injection (FdiaGenerator._load_tables). The two sets cover every bus, so every bus carries P and Q injection meters. On IEEE-14 the plan meters |V| and theta at 9 buses, P and Q at 14 buses, and 18 of 20 branch flows.

Each reading is the true value plus a constant per-meter bias plus a fresh per-scan jitter (emit_from_state). The accuracy-class standard deviations follow [ASP14] (FdiaGenerator.__init__, self.SD):

channel total std kind P_inj, Q_inj, P_from, Q_from 0.017 relative to the reading |V| 0.0012 pu absolute theta 0.00168 rad absolute

A branch current (hybrid meters) carries the PMU class of IEEE C37.118.1, a total vector error of at most 1% taken as three standard deviations, relative to the current's magnitude on the real and the imaginary part alike, plus a 1e-5 pu floor (formulas.noise.current_sigma, PMU_CURRENT_CLASS) [C37118]; its bias is drawn once per channel after the other meters' biases.

formulas.noise.bias_jitter_split splits each total into jitter 0.25 SD and bias sqrt(1 - 0.25^2) SD, so the two add to the class total in quadrature. The bias is drawn once per meter (_meter_bias). Power and flow jitter also carry an absolute floor of 1e-3 MW or MVAr, so a near-zero reading still has noise. Treating the whole class error as per-scan noise would over-jitter one-minute traces and hide the temporal signal (bias_jitter_split docstring).

docs.title: 3. The attack families
docs.text:
The two families are local false states: the attacker changes loads (and, for Am, generator outputs) inside a subnetwork, solves that subnetwork with the boundary voltages held true, and adds a = h(x_false) - h(x_true) to the true scan (engine/attacks/stealthy._stealthy_frame, engine/attacks/overload.py). Every meter keeps its own noise draw, so the residual test sees noise only. Every false state must also stay within the case's bus voltage limits and the generator P and Q limits widened to the range the pool used (engine/attacks/false_state._within_limits, operating_limits). They satisfy equations (13)-(25) of [WU26] (the SCADA measurements, the PMU voltage magnitudes, angles and branch currents, the operating limits and the line-overload goal) and its objective, eq. (12): each episode is held on the support that tampers the fewest devices (decisions D1 to D17 of the plan).

family code construction magnitude per bus episode length stealthy target set At 5 slow ramp: one load factor on a fixed bus set, rise, hold, return, each frame a local false state on the fewest-tamper support 0.2% per frame (ramp_rate), peak 2.4% to 5.2% 60 frames (ramp_len) yes 5 stealthy loads (draw_ramp) Am 7 the overload attack of [WU26]: one or two lines' reported flow driven to their ratings over the window, on the fewest-tamper support the least-norm false state that meets the goal 60 frames (am_len defaults to ramp_len) yes the rated, metered lines of the window (eligible_lines)

The codes of the single-snapshot families of older releases (1 Aq, 2 Ad, 3 As, 4 Ar, 6 Al) stay in the read-only label table fg.FAMILIES; fdia-graph 0.20 describes and generates them.

Both families run on the fewest-tamper search. Am is the overload attack of [WU26, eqs. 24-25] (engine/attacks/overload.py): at onset, the eligible branches (rated, flow metered, true flow below the rating at every snapshot of the window) are tried in a random order, and the first whose fewest-tamper support meets the goal at every snapshot is the episode's target. Snapshot t's goal is the true flow plus a linear share of what separates the window's last true flow from the rating, S_true_t + (t - kappa)/T (S_max - S_true_{kappa+T}) (the plan's D9), on the noiseless reading of the false state, reaching the rating S_max at the last snapshot; the attackable loads of the support are free, every other bus keeps its injection, and the false state is the least-norm voltage change that meets the flow. The ratings are by default 1.25 times each branch's peak true apparent flow over the operating pool (am_attack=OverloadSettings(rating_margin=...), the plan's D15), which works on every system; the PGLib-OPF ratings are the alternative, am_attack=OverloadSettings(rating_source="pglib") (IEEE-14, 118 and 300; other cases raise NoLineRatings). The generators of the support are free inside their limits, like its attackable loads, and the flow solve enforces the voltage and generator limits by an active set (the plan's D14); the limits bind every generator the attack moves, on the support's edge too, and every load bus it moves shows at most load_cap (0.5, OverloadSettings(load_cap=...)) times its true load [YUA11] (D16). Each episode overloads two lines at once, as [WU26]'s case studies do, drawn so one held support reaches both (OverloadSettings(n_lines=1) for one; D17); episodes/am_* holds one row per target line. OverloadSettings(support_method="rref") picks the support by [WU26]'s own method instead of the search: row reduction of the transposed attack-area Jacobian with column exchanges (p. 655 and Sec. IV-D1, after [YAN17]; engine/attacks/rref.py), the sparsest attack that moves each target line at every snapshot joined over the window, grown by the next sparsest rows when the AC solve cannot reach the goal on it (ours). It is much faster on IEEE-14 and tampers more devices than the search (experiment wu26.method_compare, docs/plans/WU_DEFENSE_PLAN.md, section 3). As in [WU26], nothing bounds how far Am moves a channel between snapshots: a device counts as tampered beyond [WU26]'s own case-study noise (0.03 pu SCADA, 0.01 pu PMU, the current channels included; formulas.noise.paper_sigma, the plan's D8 and D11), and the attack is stealthy because every snapshot is one AC state. At keeps its bound, each step within the meters' rated accuracy (D7). Before D11 Am carried a between-snapshot bound as well, under which no overload window was stealthy: moving one line's flow moves the injections and flows around its ends by several times that change, beyond the rated accuracy of the small loads there. A window with no stealthy overload moves the episode to another free onset of its split, earlier or later, up to 20 times (generation.design.AmDesigner: the Am of a split are designed before it is walked); past that it is given up and counted in episode_shortfall. With the hybrid meters the attacker also writes the PMU branch currents its false state moves, which counts in the PMU of the bus at that end. Only At's channels are bounded between snapshots, the currents included (the PMU class, D7); Am's current channels are only counted when they move by more than 0.01 pu (D8, D11).

The overload episodes these recipes build, measured on the hybrid meters with families=("Am",), seed 1, the pool ratings computed over the frames walked (IEEE-14 and IEEE-118 timelines of 3,000 and 2,000 frames; IEEE-30 a smoke run), before the search speed-up of #163 (experiment generation.am_overload; every line of every built episode reaches its rating):

system recipe frames episodes fallen back devices (mean) channels (mean) largest change, pu (median / max episode) s per episode IEEE-14 one line, before the D16 bounds 3000 25 0 5.3 15.0 0.18 / 5.74 15 IEEE-14 one line, D16 bounds 3000 25 0 3.9 9.9 0.14 / 0.82 30 IEEE-14 two lines, D16 bounds (default) 3000 25 0 6.8 19.3 0.17 / 1.59 39 IEEE-30 one line, before the D16 bounds 600 5 0 3.8 8.8 0.09 / 0.29 20 IEEE-118 one line, before the D16 bounds 2000 17 0 6.8 21.4 1.05 / 44.94 43 IEEE-118 one line, D16 bounds 2000 17 0 9.6 30.4 0.40 / 3.29 71 IEEE-118 two lines, D16 bounds (default) 2000 17 0 17.8 72.0 1.33 / 3.39 78

Notes on the table:

  • A stealthy target is an attackable load that is not on a generator bus, zero-MW condensers included [BOY22] (_load_tables, stealthy_pos). An attackable load has nonzero active power, is not on the slack bus and is at most max_load_mw = 2000 MW (attackable_pos).
  • The At rise lasts 20% to 45% of the episode and the hold 0% to 25% (draw_ramp). Every frame carries at least one ramp_rate of change, so every frame labelled At is attacked (EpisodeDesignMixin.ramp_step).
  • A ramp step with no local solution is halved, up to 6 times (STEP_HALVINGS). At designs are tested on every frame they will occupy before they are accepted, up to 40 draws (ONSET_DRAWS).
  • An overload Am window's snapshots are kappa+1 ... kappa+T after the untouched reference kappa [WU26, eq. 25], so its first snapshot already carries 1/T of the way to the rating and every frame labelled Am is attacked (the plan's D9). Before this fix the first snapshot's goal was the true flow and that frame tampered nothing.

docs.title: 4. Episode placement
docs.text:
step rule source split chronological, cut before anything is placed: train round(0.6 T) frames, val round(0.2 T), test the rest (split=, validated by SplitSettings) plan.split_bounds count per split, the whole number of episodes whose frames come closest to attacked_frac of its frames (whole episodes, so a short split can be off by one or two), shared between the families by largest remainder over the weights 1 / length, so every family gets about the same share of attacked frames plan.whole_episode_counts, plan.largest_remainder place per split, longest first, each at an onset drawn uniformly among the positions where it fits inside the split, never overlapping and never cut; a placement that jams is retried whole 10 times, then one episode of the family that jammed is dropped and recorded (RuntimeWarning) plan.place_split, plan.uniform_onset walk every frame emitted in time order, its meter jitter from its own stream keyed by the seed and the timestep: benign runs between episodes, each episode where it was placed emit.Walk.walk_split, MeasurementMixin._jitter_stream move an episode with no feasible design at its onset moves, up to 20 times, then is given up and recorded (RuntimeWarning): an overload Am to an onset drawn uniformly among every free one of its split, earlier or later, since the design stage designs a split's Am before any of its frames is written and an Am design reads no earlier frame (no stealth bound, D11); a ramp At to a later free onset, since its design reads the frame before its onset and the walk has written the frames before the failed one. The moves draw from streams keyed by the seed, the split, the episode and the move, so they do not depend on the workers design.AmDesigner, emit.Walk.relocate_later fallback a frame inside a built episode whose own scan cannot be built is emitted benign; the count is the fallback_benign attribute TimelineWriter.finish record the split fractions and sizes, the attacked fraction each split reached, and per split and family the episodes requested, built, moved, dropped and short TimelineWriter.finish

Adjacent episodes and long quiet stretches are outcomes of the uniform draw, not of a rule. Placing the longest episodes first keeps a long episode from being squeezed out by shorter ones. The default attacked_frac = 0.5 gives a balanced file: on a 72,000-frame timeline with 60-frame episodes every split is half attacked, up to an overload window that stays infeasible after its 20 moves. The full IEEE-14 builds of the three release datasets (seed 123, experiment generation.split_first; episodes and redraws per family, At / Am):

dataset split frames attacked episodes asked built redraws shortfall At train 43200 0.500 360 360 0 0 At val 14400 0.500 120 120 0 0 At test 14400 0.500 120 120 0 0 At build 10 min Am train 43200 0.500 360 360 88 0 Am val 14400 0.496 120 119 32 1 Am test 14400 0.500 120 120 26 0 Am build 413 min At+Am train 43200 0.500 180 / 180 180 / 180 0 / 32 0 / 0 At+Am val 14400 0.500 60 / 60 60 / 60 0 / 18 0 / 0 At+Am test 14400 0.500 60 / 60 60 / 60 0 / 15 0 / 0 At+Am build 234 min

Because the jitter of frame t depends only on the seed and t, the files of one seed and pool that place different families (families=("Am",), ("At", "Am"), ("At",)) carry byte-identical benign frames; only the attacks differ.

docs.title: Designing in parallel
docs.text:
The overload Am dominates generation time: each episode runs the fewest-tamper search on up to AM_LINE_TRIES line pairs. A split's Am episodes are independent (a flow goal reads only its own window, and each design draws its line order from a stream keyed by the seed, the split, the episode and the move), so workers=N designs them in N processes and the file is byte-identical for any N. On Windows a script that passes workers above 1 must start under if __name__ == "__main__":, as any program using multiprocessing must. An Am-only IEEE-14 timeline (experiment generation.parallel_design):

workers (3000 frames) seconds speed-up Am episodes same file 1 754 1.0x 25 yes 16 253 3.0x 25 yes

docs.title: 5. The per-frame layers
docs.text:
group datasets meaning written by data/ node_x [T, N, 4], edge_x [T, E, 2] observed readings: benign plus noise, plus the attack where attacked TimelineWriter.store data/ node_m, edge_m the meter plan per frame TimelineWriter._write_masks data/ y [T, N] 1 on each attacked bus store data/ family, stealthy, seq_id, timestep, split [T] family code, 1 for a stealthy family (At, Am; Aq and Al in older releases), episode index (-1 benign), pool timestep, 0/1/2 TimelineWriter.finish data/ temporal_delta, swing [T, N, 2] temporal features from the observed frames TimelineWriter.write_temporal_layers benign/ node_benign, edge_benign the same scan with the attack removed and the same noise draw store clean/ node_clean, edge_clean the noiseless pool state and the exact flows on metered branches IeeeSource._clean attack/ node_tamper, edge_tamper 1 where the attacker wrote the meter _store_attack data/, benign/, attack/ pmu_i, pmu_i_m, pmu_i_benign, pmu_i_tamper [T, E, 4] hybrid meters only: the PMU branch currents (Re and Im of I_from, then of I_to, per unit), their mask, the attack-removed twin, and 1 where the attacker wrote the channel _store_currents, _write_masks attack/ mag_ptr, mag_bus, mag designed change per attacked bus, ragged by frame TimelineWriter.finish episodes/ onset, length, family, bus_ptr, bus_idx one row per episode TimelineWriter.finish

node_x - node_benign is the attack exactly, for every family. The loader derives edge_clean_full, the clean flow on every branch, at read time (dataset/__init__.py).

The temporal features are written after the walk from data/node_x alone (generation.write.TimelineWriter.write_temporal_layers, formulas.temporal):

feature definition temporal_delta [P_inj, Q_inj](t) - [P_inj, Q_inj](t-1) of the observed frames; zero on frame 0 swing temporal_delta divided by the bus's recent-change scale scale std of the observed scan-to-scan absolute change over the last SWING_WINDOW = 60 changes before t, plus 1e-3; 1e-3 alone with fewer than three changes (recent_change_scale)

A spike reads as a large swing at its first frame. The slow ramp At changes by less than the typical recent change on every frame, so its swing stays near the benign level (formulas/temporal.py).

docs.title: 6. The rule for features
docs.text:
At test time a feature may use only measurements and quantities derived from them. The clean and benign layers exist for evaluation and for fitting, never as feature inputs. y, family, stealthy, seq_id, the tamper masks and the magnitudes are labels.

SDK path reads layer role SEBase.estimate node_x, edge_x measurements SEBase.fit(calibrate="truth") node_x, edge_x, family, clean fitting for the estimation benchmark: meter sigmas, benign mean state, theta_ref SEBase.fit(calibrate="measured") node_x, edge_x, family fitting from the meters' accuracy classes and the estimated benign states SEBase.score node_x, edge_x (through estimate), then family, clean the estimate from measurements, then evaluation against the truth JacobianFeatures, JacobianWeighting node_x, edge_x, prev_node_x, prev_edge_x, prev_timestep measurements GatedPrior(GateConfig(gate="oracle")) y evaluation ceiling only SwingThreshold, DeltaThreshold swing, temporal_delta measurements ResidualLocalizer node_x, edge_x measurements BusCNN, BusMLP, FedBusCNN, FedBusMLP node_x, node_m, edge_x, temporal_delta, swing, prev_swing, prev_*; y as the training label measurements TrustSelector.fit node_x, edge_x, family measurements TrustSelector.score benign, edge_benign evaluation: what a secured meter reads trust.secured.secured_copy benign, the tamper masks builds a counterfactual file, then rewrites the temporal features from its observed frames

Sources: se/base.py, se/jacobian.py, se/methods.py, localization/methods.py, localization/learned.py (_fields), trust/base.py, trust/secured.py. Every path whose output feeds a detector (ResidualLocalizer, the Jacobian feature sets, TrustSelector) fits its estimator with calibrate="measured", so no clean layer is read at fit or test time. The state estimators themselves default to calibrate="truth", the estimation benchmark's calibration.

docs.title: Where each piece lives
docs.text:
The generator is FdiaGenerator in engine/core.py, composed of mixins over the shared state contract of engine/base.py:

file holds engine/core.py FdiaGenerator: the grid, the meter plan and noise, attack targeting, and the mixins below composed engine/base.py GridBase: the attributes and cross-method signatures the mixins share engine/measurement.py MeasurementMixin: the measurement function h(x), a scan from a state engine/physics.py a scan's load and generation, read from its stored state engine/records.py one scan of the timeline writer: benign, or attacked by engine.attacks engine/solvers.py the optimization solver the AC optimal power flows run on, found and checked in one place engine/pandapower_types.py the pandapower objects the engine reads, as types engine/attacks/area.py the attacker's area: the subnetwork a stealthy attack re-solves and the boundary it holds engine/attacks/false_state.py the local false state: the area re-solved under false loads with the boundary held true engine/attacks/stealthy.py At one scan at a time: a local false state added to the true scan engine/attacks/overload.py Am, the multi-snapshot overload attack of [WU26] engine/attacks/minimize.py the cheapest support of an attack window [WU26, eq. 12] engine/attacks/rref.py the support by [WU26]'s row reduction engine/attacks/episodes.py each episode's design, drawn at onset: ramp_design and am_overload_design, methods of the generator generation/plan.py, generation/design.py, generation/emit.py, generation/write.py the stages of a timeline: plan the splits and episodes, design the Am episodes, emit every frame, write the file

The New York grid's attacks are separate classes on the New York network: engine/attacks/attacker.py (Attacker), engine/attacks/family.py (the interface of an attack family; its design is an Episode, models/plan.py), engine/attacks/ramp.py (Ramp), engine/attacks/opf.py and engine/attacks/interface.py (the overload of an interface, with false states from a local optimal power flow); they are described in ../concepts/new_york_grid.md.

docs.title: 7. Building your own
docs.text:
import fdia_graph as fg

fg.generate("ieee118", name="my_run", frames=10_000, attacked_frac=0.5)  # needs [generate]
ds = fg.load("my_run", order="time")

generation.generate(system, name, frames=None, states=None, out=None, seed=123, settings=None, **knobs) loads the pool, keeps the first frames timesteps, calls timeline.generate_timeline and registers the file under name. Without states, it reads $FDIA_GRAPH_INIT or downloads the system's pool.

knob default meaning attacked_frac 0.5 fraction of frames under an episode families ("At", "Am") the families in rotation; the single-snapshot families of older releases are refused min_tamper True hold each episode on the support that tampers the fewest devices [WU26, eq. 12] am_attack "overload" Am as the overload attack of [WU26], or an OverloadSettings stealth_scale 1.0 a multiplier on At's stealth bound, in units of the rated accuracy (Am has none, D11) redundancy MeterSettings() the meter plan, a MeterSettings: coverage vbus_frac 0.6, pmu_frac 0.2, flow_frac 0.9, and meter_model "hybrid" (D10, D12) ramp_rate 0.002 At growth per frame ramp_len 60 At episode length am_len ramp_len Am episode length hops 2 the attacker's subnetwork reach in branches split (0.6, 0.2, 0.2) chronological train/val/test fractions max_load_mw 2000.0 a larger load is never a target; None disables seed 123 the meter plan, the biases and every attack draw workers 1 processes the overload Am designs run on; the file does not depend on it

Every knob is also a field of TimelineSettings, nested by subject (ramp, search, overload, meters, split): generate(..., settings=TimelineSettings(ramp=RampSettings(length=30))), with any flat knob applied over it. The file records the settings it ran as JSON (attribute settings) with their hash (settings_hash).

A data release (the build scripts of v0.8.0 to v0.8.3 are in the git history at aa77d0b):

  1. Per system, copy the unchanged pool and run fg.generate(C, ..., states=pool, seed=123, frames=72000) into timeline_ieee{C}.h5; each system writes a manifest fragment with sha256 and size.
  2. Run once more with MERGE=1 to combine the fragments into manifest.json.
  3. Upload with python tools/upload_assets.py vX.Y.Z notes.md <files>; it creates the data-vX.Y.Z tag and never replaces an asset already on the release.
  4. Add the release's sha256 values to registry._SHA256, then bump registry._RELEASE last.

docs.title: The New York grid: building the timeline
docs.text: fdia_graph.generation.nygrid builds a federated FDIA timeline on the New York grid: NYgrid's modified NPCC-140 case in AC, a 2019 five-minute operating-point pool from a ramp-constrained AC dispatch, one client per utility service territory, a hybrid SCADA and PMU meter plan, and attacks against NYISO interface limits. The modules are in the architecture, one run end to end in the walkthrough, how to add an attack or an alarm rule in the extending guide, and what each stage reports when it fails in the troubleshooting page. No built pool or timeline is published yet, so the steps below build them from the public inputs.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
The build tools live in the repository's pipelines/newyork/, not in the wheel, so work from a checkout:

git clone https://github.com/myersben9/fdia-graph && pip install -e "./fdia-graph[ny]"
conda install -c conda-forge ipopt   # the AC dispatch solves through Pyomo with Ipopt
export FG=$PWD/fdia-graph

The steps below run in a separate work folder that holds the inputs and the outputs.

docs.title: 1. Inputs
docs.text:
mkdir nygrid && cd nygrid
python $FG/pipelines/newyork/build_timeline.py --fetch

The grid itself needs no download: it is the MATPOWER case file shipped with the package (nygrid_case()). fetch_inputs writes data/: NYgrid's Data/ folder at commit 47698b6 (its hourly 2019 data), NYISO's 2019 five-minute zonal load, the NYS DPS utility territories, and the bus locations that place each New York bus in a territory (shipped with the package). The building-stock load profiles, EIA-861 and the industrial assessment database are downloaded by the load model the first time the pool is built (about 200 MB, 15 minutes). Every step keeps a file that is already there.

docs.title: 2. The operating-point pool
docs.text:
python $FG/pipelines/newyork/run_pool.py 2019-01-01 2020-01-01 out/pool_2019.h5 --workers 8

The year is dispatched in weekly chunks in parallel, then each seam between chunks is solved again until the dispatch is continuous. The pool holds the true state and injections of every five-minute frame.

docs.title: 3. The timeline
docs.text:
python $FG/pipelines/newyork/build_timeline.py out/timeline_2019.h5 --pool out/pool_2019.h5 --workers 8

The script builds the release's source and generates it: NewYorkSource.production(pool_path, NewYorkRelease(...)).generate(path). generate is the one path every timeline takes, the IEEE ones too (generation.md). The file is written as timeline_2019.h5.part and takes its name when it is whole, so a build that stops leaves no file to mistake for a timeline. The design processes are spawned: a script of your own that asks for more than one worker must start under if __name__ == "__main__":. NewYorkSource.production puts every decided bound in one place: line ratings from the pool's peak flows, the overload attack (Am) against the Sprain Brook/Dunwoodie South interface, the slow ramp (At), 20% of each split's frames attacked, and onsets surveyed among the hours an attack can reach. The weeks are split into train, validation and test, stratified on those hours.

For one attack studied by hand, pipelines/newyork/build_single_episodes.py OUT_DIR --pool out/pool_2019.h5 --onset 2019-07-05T10:30:00 writes the whole day of that onset with a single Am episode in it.

docs.title: 4. Reading it as clients
docs.text:
from fdia_graph.dataset.clients import Dataset

ds = Dataset("out/timeline_2019.h5")
con_ed = ds.client("ConEd", split="train")  # only this utility's meters, buses and labels
x = con_ed.node_features()  # [T, N_c, 4] metered |V|, angle, P, Q per owned bus
op = ds.operator(split="test")  # every meter, for state estimation

A client sees only its own meters and the labels of its own buses. The operator view is the full scan.

The file has the layout of every timeline (fdia_graph.schema; the table is in new_york_grid.md), so fg.FdiaGraph("out/timeline_2019.h5") opens it too: the static graph, the admittance matrices and the layers per frame. Dataset is the view by meter and by client: ds.plan is the meter table, ds.z(frames) the flat reading vector of that table, ds.z(frames, benign=True) the same scans without the attack and ds.tampered(frames) the tampered meters. A file written before this layout is refused; it reads with fdia-graph 0.21.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
tests/nygrid reads the inputs and the pool under NYGRID_ROOT (the folder of steps 1 to 3) and skips a test whose input is missing:

NYGRID_ROOT=/path/to/nygrid pytest $FG/tests/nygrid

Most tests need only the inputs of step 1, with the pool frames of two days checked in under tests/nygrid/data/days; the tests that rate lines or survey onsets over the year also need the pool of step 2. tests/nygrid/inputs.py says which input each test needs. CI runs the folder on the inputs of step 1 (.github/workflows/nygrid.yml).

docs.title: Beating WLS: state estimation with the SDK
docs.text: Measurements in, state out, better than weighted least squares on the public test cases. Runs off the default timeline download (data release v0.8.3); pip install "fdia-analysis[se]".

docs.title: Baseline first
docs.text:
import fdia_graph as fg
from fdia_analysis.se.methods import WLS

train, test = fg.load("ieee14", split="train"), fg.load("ieee14", split="test")
wls = WLS().fit(train)
xhat = wls.estimate(test)  # [n, 2N-1] = [theta rad (non-slack) | V pu (all buses)]
print(wls.score(test).geo)  # angle_mae_deg, voltage_mae_pu (docs/analysis/estimation/README.md has the table)
fit() learns estimate() returns per-meter error scales: RMS of benign residuals at the dataset's clean truth (the benchmark default, calibrate="truth"), or each meter's accuracy class from measurements alone (calibrate="measured", what every detector path uses); the reference angle theta_ref the classical 2N-1 state, every voltage magnitude and every non-slack angle the chord Jacobian at the benign mean state in one angle frame: the slack angle is fixed to theta_ref, taken from the training truth at fit time (the case's reference angle on the released pools)

docs.title: The better estimator
docs.text:
from fdia_analysis.models.config import PriorConfig
from fdia_analysis.se.methods import SubspacePrior

est = SubspacePrior(prior=PriorConfig(rank_frac=0.2, reweight="huber", c=1.5)).fit(train)
print(est.score(test).geo)  # about half WLS's angle error on IEEE-14 (the table below)
piece does why it helps prior restricts the estimate to the low-rank subspace benign operation occupies (SVD of the training states) learns generator voltage setpoints from history instead of re-estimating them from noisy meters every scan Huber down-weights measurements the physics cannot explain rejects in-place meter corruption together on IEEE-14 test 45% lower angle error, 81% lower voltage error than WLS geometric mean over the eight record classes (benign and seven families), v0.8.3 timeline

Validation-selected hyperparameters from the estimation paper:

system rank_frac Huber c ResidualRemoval threshold ieee14 0.20 1.5 4.0 ieee118 0.50 2.5 5.0 ieee300 0.50 6.0 none helps

docs.title: PMU pseudo-measurements
docs.text:
On a hybrid-meter file (new generation) a SCADA voltmeter reads no angle, so the angle comes from the PMUs and the power meters alone. pmu_pseudo=True (every estimator, JacobianWeighting included, which reads the previous frame's currents from prev_pmu_i) adds the pseudo-measurements of [WU26, eq. (3)]: a PMU at the near end n of a branch reads V_n and I_n, and the branch's pi model gives the voltage at the far end f,

V_f = (I_n - y_nn V_n) / y_nf

with y_nn, y_nf the branch's Y_f or Y_t entries (taps and phase shifts included), averaged over the branches that reach f (formulas.estimation.pmu_pseudo_voltages). The pseudo |V| and angle fill the slots of the reached buses that no meter reads; a SCADA |V| is kept where one exists. Their first-order error, with independent PMU errors, is the covariance of

dV_f = R(1/y_nf) dI_n - R(y_nn/y_nf) P_n (d|V_n|, dtheta_n)

(R(c) the real 2x2 matrix of multiplying by c, P_n the polar-to-rectangular Jacobian at V_n), summed over the links with the voltage terms grouped by PMU bus, then carried to |V_f| and theta_f through the rectangular-to-polar gradients; for a round error of complex variance s^2 this is var|V_f| = s^2 / 2 and var theta_f = s^2 / (2 |V_f|^2). calibrate="measured" weights the pseudo slots by that variance, calibrate="truth" by their benign residual like every other slot. The formula is exact without noise (to 1e-16 on IEEE-14 and 118) and its variance matches a Monte Carlo of 20,000 draws to within 3% (analysis/tests/test_pmu_channels.py).

Measured with WLS on the test split, with only the meter model changed: taking the angles away from the SCADA voltmeters raises the benign angle error, and the eq. (3) pseudo-measurements win part of it back. The comparison is rerun into the results store with the v0.9.0 data; its earlier numbers had no stored run behind them and are not repeated here.

docs.title: What to expect per family
docs.text:
records behaviour why At, Am (stealthy, and Aq, Al in older releases) robust weighting sees nothing; the prior moves them part of the way a consistent AC state leaves no residual, and it sits off the benign operating subspace, so the prior pulls the estimate part of the way back Ad bias, As scaling, Ar replay (older releases only) improve a lot meters corrupted in place, which robust weighting exists to reject benign improves on the larger systems, can lose slightly on ieee14 the baseline is already at the noise floor there

Full per-family table and figures, on data release v0.8.x: ../analysis/estimation/README.md.

docs.title: Your own estimator
docs.text:
Subclass SEBase and override one hook; the rest is shared, so comparisons are estimator against estimator.

hook does _fit_states(x_benign) learn anything from the benign training states _subspace() a [2N-1, K] basis that restricts the state space, or None for the full state _solve(z, w) the per-batch solve; w is per-record weights [n, m], or None for the shared ones

Inside _solve: self._w_solve(z, w) is the divergence-guarded weighted iteration, self._nres(x, z) the normalized residuals, and formulas.estimation holds every equation (huber_weights, wls_step, normalized_residual, ...).

docs.title: The New York grid: how it fails
docs.text: Every stage of fdia_graph.generation.nygrid either raises a named error or records why it produced less than asked. This page lists what each stage reports, what it means and what to do. The stages are those of the guide: environment, inputs, the operating-point pool and the timeline. The errors live in fdia_graph.errors. A wrong argument is a ConfigError and data that does not meet a condition is a DataConditionError. Both are a ValueError, so existing except ValueError code keeps working. SolverUnavailable is a RuntimeError, because a broken environment is not a property of the data.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text: What you see Why Fix SolverUnavailable: Ipopt is not found or does not start Ipopt is not installed, or it is installed but cannot load its DLLs. On Windows a missing DLL shows as exit code 0xC0000135 conda install -c conda-forge ipopt into the environment, and run that environment's Python with the environment active, so its Library/bin folder is on PATH. fdia_graph.engine.solvers.ipopt() adds the folder when it exists SolverUnavailable: Pyomo is not installed The [ny] extra is missing pip install "fdia-graph[ny]" A change you made does not show up Python imports another copy of the package, usually the editable install of the main checkout when you work in a git worktree Put the worktree's src first: PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/src FileNotFoundError on data/... The build tools read data/ and out/ relative to the working folder Run from the work folder that holds data/, or pass --data and --pool

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: What you see Why Fix DataConditionError: bus ... has no row in ... A bus of the case has no location in the bus-location table Re-fetch the inputs (build_timeline.py --fetch). The table ships with the package DataConditionError: ...: branch f-t is not in the case in that orientation An interface definition names a branch the case does not hold The case or the interface table changed; check both against the NYgrid commit the guide pins DataConditionError: ...: no rows in interflowHourly_<year>.csv No interface flows for that year Fetch the inputs for the year you build

docs.title: The operating-point pool
docs.text:
PoolBuilder.report() counts every frame by its solve kind. Only solved frames are used downstream.

Solve kind Meaning What to do solved The dispatch and the AC power flow converged Nothing failed The dispatch or the power flow did not converge for that frame A few per year are expected (the 2019 pool solves 99.8 percent). Many in a row point at the inputs of those hours no_hour The hour a chunk starts from has no AC point, so the chunk has no start Usually follows a failed hour; rebuild that span no_load NYISO has no load for the frame (the spring-forward gap and data gaps) Nothing; these frames are skipped everywhere

report() before build() raises NotFitted. A span whose first hour has no AC point raises a DataConditionError naming the frame.

docs.title: The timeline
docs.text:
After source.generate(path), NewYorkSource.summary() returns a summary. When the build made fewer attacks than it placed, missed (and, with the onset survey on, survey_missed) says why, counted per family:

Reason Meaning What to do no_target The window has nothing to attack: no line or interface near its limit, or no load bus for a ramp Expected outside the near-limit hours. If it covers every slot, the onset mask and the interface data disagree infeasible Targets existed, but no support met every bound of the attacker (load cap, basepoint band, ramps, voltage limits) The bounds are binding. Widening them is a modeling decision, not a fix solver_error Ipopt started but stopped abnormally on a support the search tried, so the window may hold an attack the search did not see A few are tolerable. Many mean a numerically hard case; the family's solver_errors counts them

For one episode alone, building the SingleEpisodeSource raises a DataConditionError when the window touches an unsolved frame, and its generate raises NoAdmissibleTarget naming the reason when that one window has no attack.

A run that fails leaves no file: the timeline is written under a .part name and takes its own only when it is whole. A build whose design processes never start, or that starts itself again and again, is a script without if __name__ == "__main__": around its entry: the processes are spawned and import the script.

docs.title: The golden snapshots
docs.text:
tests/nygrid/test_golden.py compares what the interface attack returns on fixed inputs with the snapshots in tests/nygrid/golden/. A failure names the first value that changed. If the change is intended, rewrite the snapshots with NYGRID_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 and say in the pull request which numbers moved and why. The interface attack's design needs the whole 2019 pool under NYGRID_ROOT and skips without it. The persistence rule's snapshot is two numbers, analysis/tests/golden/persistence_rule.json, compared by analysis/tests/test_detect.py; it needs no data, and an intended change edits the file.

The same folder holds whole-file digests of a New York timeline and of two episodes (tests/nygrid/test_timeline_digests.py): bit for bit on the machine that recorded them, skipped elsewhere. Rewrite those with FDIA_UPDATE_DIGESTS=1, under the same rule.

docs.title: Benchmarks
docs.text:
Per-record timings on the tiny IEEE-14 timeline, stored by python tools/bench.py as a run of the results store's bench experiment (results/bench.csv) and rendered below by tools/results_docs.py; --check fails when a timing is more than 3x slower than the last run. One machine's rows are comparable with each other, not with another machine's.

From 0.18 the generate column is milliseconds per timeline frame of the test suite's tiny timeline (TIMELINE_KW in tests/helpers.py, 1000 frames); earlier rows timed the record-shard writer per record and are not comparable to it.

From 0.20 that timeline has one-frame Aq and Al episodes, and its seed moved with them, so a later row's generate column times a different episode mix from the rows above it. From 0.21 it holds At and the overload Am only on the hybrid meters (seed 2, the search capped at 16 supports): other frames and another meter plan, so none of its columns, the estimators' included, compares with the rows above. tools/bench.py records the fixture recipe with each row, starts a new table for a new recipe, and --check compares only rows of the same machine and recipe; the first run on this recipe starts its baseline.

date generate ms/record wls ms/record huber ms/record prior+huber ms/record version machine recipe 2026-09-16 79.839 0.110 2.824 1.885 0.17.0 AMD64 Intel64 Family 6 Model 143 Stepping 8, GenuineIntel, numpy 1.26.4, torch 2.12.0.dev20260314+cu128 shards

docs.title: The fewest-tamper search
docs.text:
Median seconds per episode of the overload (Am) and ramp (At) search, before and after a change, run side by side on the same fixed episodes (seed 1, hybrid meters, pool ratings, the D16 bounds, two-line Am, budget 256, 20-snapshot windows; experiment search.speed). Every episode returned the same answer before and after.

The search speed-up (#163):

system default threads, Am default threads, At one thread, Am one thread, At IEEE-14 (10 Am, 4 At) 4.5 to 3.0 0.84 to 0.66 4.5 to 2.9 0.36 to 0.21 IEEE-30 (5 Am, 3 At) 8.5 to 4.8 1.1 to 0.98 8.4 to 5.1 0.54 to 0.41 IEEE-118 (4 Am, 3 At) 14.5 to 9.5 1.8 to 0.98 5.2 to 3.3 1.1 to 0.44

BLAS held to one thread during the search (#164):

system default threads, Am default threads, At one thread, Am one thread, At IEEE-14 (10 Am, 4 At) 3.1 to 3.1 0.58 to 0.28 3.0 to 2.7 0.31 to 0.31 IEEE-30 (5 Am, 3 At) 5.5 to 5.6 0.81 to 0.33 5.5 to 5.1 0.32 to 0.26 IEEE-118 (4 Am, 3 At) 7.2 to 3.1 0.89 to 0.44 3.3 to 3.3 0.38 to 0.51

docs.title: Class map
docs.text:
How the pieces of the two toolkits connect, the generation toolkit fdia_graph and the analysis toolkit fdia_analysis: one module diagram of both and eight class diagrams, all drawn from the source by tools/class_diagrams.py (the AST gives each class's public methods, its bases and the classes of other modules it names), so they cannot drift from the code. CI checks that the committed sources match; python tools/class_diagrams.py rewrites them and tools/render_mermaid.py renders. Read with ROADMAP.md (what each file is for) and CONCEPTS_TO_CODE.md (which function implements which idea).

An open arrowhead is inheritance, a dashed arrow is a class using another (an argument type, a return type or a collaborator it builds), and a box marked with another package's name is a participant that lives there.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text: Which module imports which, in one picture with a box per toolkit: every arrow between the boxes runs from the analysis toolkit to the generation toolkit, never back. Four foundations are read by nearly every module and are left out so the real dependencies show: each toolkit's models/ (the returned records and the settings; the one validation engine is fdia_graph.models.validation) and formulas/ (the equations), and the generation toolkit's schema.py (the file protocol) and errors.py (the named errors). Each package's own __init__.py (for fdia_graph, the fg.* public API, which imports everything) is left out for the same reason.

docs.title: The dataset
docs.text: FdiaGraph is the file. Five mixins over DatasetBase give it its faces: the static graph physics (GraphMixin), the admittance matrices (AdmittanceMixin), records and batches (RecordsMixin), the exports (ExportMixin) and the time-ordered windows and episodes (SequenceMixin). The methods that produce records return models bundles (a record, a batch, an exported split, the episode table, the summary); the graph properties are tensors or arrays, loader() is a DataLoader and windows() a tuple.

docs.title: The engine
docs.text: FdiaGenerator is the AC model of one system with its meter plan. GridBase declares what the mixins provide: MeasurementMixin emits scans, PhysicsMixin re-solves the whole grid under new loads and reads a scan's load and generation, and AttackMixin builds every attack (next section). engine/records.py emits a benign scan and hands an attacked family to the mixin; timeline.py decides when and where each episode runs.

docs.title: The attacks
docs.text: Every attack is built in engine/attacks/, one module per concern, composed into AttackMixin: AreaMixin finds the attacker's area, FalseStateMixin solves and checks its false state and the attack vector, StealthyMixin builds the ramp frames, MinimizeMixin finds the support that tampers the fewest devices over an attack window [WU26, eq. 12], OverloadMixin builds the overload Am, and EpisodeDesignMixin draws what an At episode attacks at its onset. AttackMixin.attack_frame is the one entry for an attacked At scan; an Am frame comes from overload_step.

docs.title: State estimation
docs.text: SEBase holds the shared solve: the measurement function, the chord Jacobian, the meter weights and the chord-Newton loop. Each estimator overrides one hook. GatedPrior takes a fitted localizer as its gate; JacobianFeatures is the per-bus feature block the localizers can consume.

docs.title: Localization and trusted meters
docs.text: LocalizerBase calibrates any per-bus score to one false-alarm budget; the threshold arms score a stored feature, ResidualLocalizer runs an estimator, the learned arms train a per-bus network. TrustSelector chooses the meters to secure on the WLS Jacobian, by row reduction (TrustedMeters) or by a deep Q-network (TrustedMetersDQN), and scores the residual test with them secured.

docs.title: Federated training
docs.text: FederatedLocalizer is a LearnedLocalizer whose fit runs FedAvg over a Partition of the buses: each client trains its own copy with the shared LocalTrainer on its own buses, and FedBusMLP and FedBusCNN take their encoder from BusMLP and BusCNN. RoundLog records every round. RegionalPrior is a SubspacePrior whose basis is fitted per client of a Partition.

docs.title: The records
docs.text: Everything a call returns is a Bundle, a dict with attribute access and a fixed key order. The record forms share seven field-group mixins, one per group of keys, so a record, a batch and an exported split carry the same names. An exported split adds an eighth, export-only group, PreviousFrameFields (the previous frame's readings on a timeline).

docs.title: The scores
docs.text:
The result of every score() is a Bundle too, defined in the analysis toolkit (fdia_analysis.models.scores) on the generation toolkit's Bundle: ErrorPair and EstimatorScores for the estimators, OverallMetrics, BenignMetrics, FamilyMetrics and LocalizerScores for the localizers, TrustScores for the trusted meters, JacobianOutputs for the feature block; TrueState (fdia_analysis.models.data) is the truth an estimator is scored against.

The named tuples of models/frames.py (Scan, Frame, OperatingLimits, FrameKnobs), models/grid.py (the column indices, BranchModel, Admittances, MeterPlan, MeterBias, Outage) and models/assets.py (AssetSpec) are plain value types with no hierarchy, so they appear only where a class above uses them.

docs.title: Concepts to code
docs.text: Paper ideas → the function that implements them. Pair with DATA_DICTIONARY.md. Paths are under src/fdia_graph/.

docs.title: One record, start to finish
docs.text: Every attack is built in engine.attacks, the generator's AttackMixin: a local false state (engine.attacks.false_state) designed per episode (ramp_design for At, am_overload_design for Am, engine.attacks.episodes) on a support the search or [WU26]'s row reduction chooses (MinimizeMixin.min_tamper, RrefSupport); engine.records.attack_frame adds the attack vector to the benign scan.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
The paper's math lives in engine/. generation/ drives it in stages (TimelineSource.generate is the one path of them for both grids, timeline.py its IEEE entry point), profiles.py turns load series into operating points; se/ and localization/ analyze the timelines; the rest load and serve data. What every file does, from its docstring, is MODULES.md (generated by tools/layout.py); FORMULAS.md maps each formula to its function.

engine/ file formula it implements core.py FdiaGenerator: grid + noise setup (__init__), attack targeting; composes the measurement, physics and attack mixins measurement.py emit_from_state (the measurement function h(x)), clean_flows_from_states, currents_from_states physics.py true_load, scan_generation: a scan's load and generation from its stored state attacks/ the false states, the fewest-tamper search, the At ramp and the overload Am

One column order everywhere: the operating-state pool, node_x, and clean are all [|V|, P_inj, Q_inj, theta]. Pools saved before 0.12 were P-first; generation.as_v_first detects and converts them on load.

docs.title: State estimation
docs.text:
concept code WLS x̂ = argmin (z−h(x))ᵀW(z−h(x)) se/base.py SEBase._w_solve (chord-Newton); h(x) is engine/measurement.emit_from_state Robust reweighting (Huber), residual removal, subspace prior se/methods.py: one class per arm, each overrides one hook Bad-data test r_i=(z_i−h_i)/σ_i, J=Σr_i² σ_i is the RMS of the benign residuals at the training truth (se/base.py SEBase.fit); residuals in se/base.py SEBase._nres. The stealthy flag marks the families that evade it by construction (Aq/At/Al/Am, models.choices.STEALTHY_FAMILIES) Noise model FdiaGenerator.SD (accuracy class): reading = true + per-meter bias + per-scan jitter. The estimator does not read it; it calibrates σ_i from data Meter model (hybrid SCADA and PMU, the plan's D10) MeasurementMixin.meter_masks (the angle at the PMU buses only), current_mask and _emit_currents (the PMU branch currents I_f = Y_f V, I_t = Y_t V, formulas.network.branch_currents, noise formulas.noise.current_sigma); chosen by generate_timeline(..., redundancy={"meter_model": ...}) through models.config.MeterSettings PMU pseudo-measurements V_f = (I_n − y_nn V_n)/y_nf [WU26, eq. (3)] formulas.estimation.pmu_pseudo_links, pmu_pseudo_voltages (with the propagated variance), used by SEBase(solve=SolveConfig(pmu_pseudo=True)) in _build_pseudo and _z_of

Walkthrough: ../guides/state_estimation.md. Results: ../analysis/estimation/README.md.

docs.title: Attack families
docs.text:
family paper build code At A_t slow ramp, 0.2 percent per frame, a local false state per frame engine/attacks/episodes.EpisodeDesignMixin.ramp_design + EpisodeDesignMixin.ramp_step Am A_m the overload attack of [WU26]: a line's reported flow driven to its rating over the window, the fewest devices tampered engine/attacks/episodes.EpisodeDesignMixin.am_overload_design + overload.overload_step
  • At and Am are local false states: the buses around the attack are re-solved with the boundary voltages held true, inside the case's voltage limits and the region's generator limits, and the attack vector h(x') − h(x) is added to the benign scan. The residual test flags them at the benign rate by construction. Both satisfy equations (13)-(23) of [WU26] (the SCADA measurements, the PMU voltage magnitudes, angles and branch currents, and the operating limits). Am also drives a line's reported flow to its rating, eqs. (24)-(25) (by default 1.25 times its peak pool flow, D15), on the support that tampers the fewest devices, eq. (12); At is held on that support when min_tamper=True (the default), else on the region within hops (../guides/generation.md, section 3). The single-snapshot families of older releases (Aq, Al, and the in-place Ad, As, Ar) are read-only: fdia-graph 0.20 generates them.
  • With min_tamper=True an At episode is held on the support that tampers the fewest devices over the episode, the objective of [WU26, eq. 12] (engine/attacks/minimize.MinimizeMixin.min_tamper, called by engine/attacks/episodes.EpisodeDesignMixin.ramp_design).
  • The At ramp moves in per-frame steps under the noise floor, by design.

docs.title: Temporal feature
docs.text:
field meaning built in temporal_delta scan-to-scan [ΔP, ΔQ] of the observed frames generation.write.TimelineWriter.write_temporal_layers (formulas.temporal.temporal_delta) swing temporal_delta as a z-score of the recent observed change generation.write.TimelineWriter.write_temporal_layers (formulas.temporal.swing_zscore, scale from recent_change_scale)

Both layers are written after the walk from the observed injections only, so a detector reads what an operator sees.

Any above-noise attack spikes the swing, so localization is per-bus and needs no graph. The slow ramp At stays inside the swing, so it is the open case.

docs.title: The papers' per-bus feature vector and localizers
docs.text: concept code 14-dim per-bus vector: [|V|,P,Q,θ] + meter mask + partial KCL residual + temporal_delta + swing localization/learned.py full14, kcl_residual standardize all 14 channels on train (sd floored at 1e-3) LearnedLocalizer._fit_stats 1-D CNN across the bus axis (best localizer) BusCNN per-bus MLP (lightweight arm) BusMLP validation-best global threshold on a 0.05..0.95 grid LearnedLocalizer.tune_threshold
